articles.title: Excel-User warten schon Jahre darauf: Microsoft hebt nervige Regel auf
articles.text:
Excel-User warten schon Jahre darauf: Microsoft hebt nervige Regel auf
Wer Excel regelmäßig nutzt, wird schon so einige Tricks und Kniffe kennen, um mehr aus dem Tabellen-Tool herauszuholen. Wer noch Nachhilfe benötigt, kann sich Tipps beim Excel-Weltmeister holen und damit potenziell Stunden im Büroalltag sparen. In jedem Fall gibt es aber schon seit Jahrzehnten eine kleine Einschränkung in Excel, die der Produktivität gelegentlich in die Quere kommen kann.
Welche Excel-Änderung Microsoft jetzt vornimmt
Fügst du in eine Zelle mehrere Begriffe oder Zahlen ein, die von Kommata getrennt werden, liest Excel diese Einträge nicht separat. Stattdessen wirft Excel sie alle zu einem einzelnen Begriff zusammen. Das ist besonders dann ärgerlich, wenn du die Begriffe als Filter für Listen nutzen willst. Bisher mussten Excel-User:innen immer den Workaround über einzelne Zellen für jeden neuen Begriff gehen. Doch das hat jetzt ein Ende, wie Windows Latest berichtet.
Mit einem neuen Update implementiert Microsoft die Funktion, Listen in eine einzelne Zelle einzufügen. Dadurch erscheinen alle Begriffe, die du hintereinander in die Zelle einfügst, trotzdem als einzelne Filteroptionen in der Tabelle. Das Einfügen von Listen in Excel-Zellen ist recht simpel. Du kannst dafür entweder eine Zelle markieren und die Tastenkombination „Strg + J“ drücken oder über das Menü „Einfügen“ die neue Listenfunktion auswählen.
Passend dazu führt Microsoft noch neue Funktionen in Excel ein, die sich um die Listen drehen. „HAS“ überprüft, ob sich ein bestimmtes Item in der Liste befindet. Dazu kommen „HASANY“ zur Prüfung, ob sich einer der ausgewählten Werte wiederfindet, und „HASALL“, bei dem alle ausgewählten Begriffe in der Liste auftauchen müssen.
Zunächst rollt Microsoft das neue Excel-Update nur an Tester:innen im Beta-Kanal des Insiderprogramms aus. Sie sollen die neuen Features zunächst auf mögliche Fehler prüfen, die Microsoft dann vor einem finalen Release beseitigen kann. Wie lange dieser Prozess dauert, hängt stark davon ab, ob beim Testen größere Bugs auftauchen oder nicht.

articles.title: Le nouvel Outlook va enfin vous empêcher d’envoyer un mail si vous avez laissé passer une faute
articles.text:
Le nouvel Outlook continue de rattraper son prédécesseur. Microsoft prépare le retour d’une option pourtant élémentaire, capable de lancer automatiquement le correcteur orthographique juste avant l’envoi d’un mail.
Microsoft aura pris son temps. Plus de trois ans après l’arrivée du nouvel Outlook, le client de messagerie va enfin récupérer une fonction présente depuis longtemps dans sa version classique : la vérification automatique de l’orthographe avant l’envoi d’un message. Le correcteur intégré signale déjà les fautes pendant la rédaction, mais rien n’empêche actuellement d’expédier un mail alors qu’il en contient encore. Une future option viendra combler cette lacune.
Outlook vérifiera vos mails une dernière fois avant leur départ
Dans le détail, le nouvel Outlook lancera automatiquement une dernière vérification orthographique au moment de cliquer sur le bouton Envoyer. Si le correcteur repère encore une faute ou un terme qu’il ne reconnaît pas, l’utilisateur ou l’utilisatrice pourra en être averti et rectifier son erreur avant que le message quitte la boîte d’envoi.
Pour rappel, le nouvel Outlook sait déjà repérer les fautes grâce à Microsoft Editor, qui les souligne au fil de la frappe et permet de les examiner depuis les outils de correction intégrés au client. Ce mode de vérification dépend toutefois de l’attention portée aux suggestions, un mot souligné pouvant facilement passer inaperçu au moment d’expédier un message.
Une nouvelle fonction qui n’en est finalement pas vraiment une, puisque Outlook classique propose depuis des années une option similaire permettant de « toujours vérifier l’orthographe avant l'envoi ». Microsoft réintroduit donc dans son nouveau client une possibilité disparue lors de sa refonte, comme il l’a déjà fait pour plusieurs fonctions laissées de côté lors du passage à la nouvelle application.
La nouvelle option restera facultative et il faudra l’activer dans les paramètres d’Outlook pour pouvoir en profiter. D’après le calendrier communiqué par Microsoft, elle commencera son déploiement auprès des utilisateurs et utilisatrices du canal Targeted Release à partir de la mi-octobre 2026. Le déploiement général débutera à la mi-novembre et se poursuivra jusqu’au début du mois de décembre, dans le nouvel Outlook pour Windows comme dans Outlook sur le web.

articles.title: Southwest and United don't want Boeing's newest 737 MAX software on their new planes
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Southwest Airlines and United Airlines have asked Boeing to deliver new 737 MAX jets with an earlier software version after the manufacturer identified a glitch involving an automated navigation function. Neither airline has aircraft flying with the affected software, according to company statements. However, both carriers have told Boeing they do not want it installed on incoming planes.
The problem can arise after a flight crew abandons a landing and changes the aircraft's planned route. Under certain conditions, an automated navigation feature may not work as intended. Pilots could then have to fly without some autopilot functions until they restore the system or continue using manual procedures.
That can add to the workload during a critical phase of flight. A missed approach typically requires a crew to climb away from the runway, follow a new route and manage the aircraft at a relatively low altitude. Weather or other operational issues may also be factors.
Boeing told 737 MAX operators about the issue in late August. The company said at the time that it did not consider the problem a safety risk. It has since started a formal safety review and shared the results with the Federal Aviation Administration.
The FAA is investigating. A senior agency official said the regulator will act if necessary.
Boeing said it had reminded operators of the existing procedures pilots can use to handle such situations safely. The company added that its engineers are developing a software update intended to permanently resolve the problem.
Boeing is also working with airlines on procedures that would allow pilots to re-enable the affected navigation function. Its August notice said more guidance was expected by November, with a software update planned for early 2028. Boeing said it is trying to move both dates forward.
GE Aerospace developed the software at issue. The company said it is working with Boeing and will support the FAA's review.
It is not yet known how many MAX aircraft have the software installed. Boeing said it is working to determine that number, but airlines are not required to tell the manufacturer when they update cockpit software. Aviation data firm Cirium lists 2,422 MAX 8 and MAX 9 aircraft in service worldwide.
Alaska Airlines, American Airlines, Southwest, and United all operate MAX jets. Those airlines said none of their active aircraft are using the software version at issue. Boeing has told carriers they can return to an earlier version.
The software issue could also affect Boeing's plans for its newest MAX variants. The FAA approved the smaller MAX 7 for passenger service last month with the newer software installed, according to a senior agency official. Boeing Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg has said he expects the MAX 10 to receive approval soon.
The FAA's findings could complicate that process. If the agency determines that the glitch is an unsafe condition that must be corrected, it could affect MAX 10 certification.
Southwest has a particular interest in the outcome. The carrier has been waiting years for the MAX 7 and plans to begin flying it next year. Federal rules generally require newly built aircraft to match the configuration approved during certification. It remains unclear whether new MAX 7s could be delivered with the earlier software Southwest has requested.
Delta Air Lines, United, American, and Alaska have MAX 10s on order.
Boeing said it first learned of the issue from a MAX operator in November 2024. The company initially concluded that the report did not meet its standard for a safety review. It reconsidered after speaking with airlines and receiving additional feedback.
The matter comes as Boeing continues to face close scrutiny of the MAX program. Crashes involving the aircraft in 2018 and 2019 killed 346 people. Those accidents involved the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System, or MCAS, which repeatedly pushed the planes' noses down. Boeing later changed the system and added safeguards before the MAX returned to service.

articles.title: Montage Technology Announces Mass Production of Gen 5 DDR5 Register Clock Driver
articles.text:
Monday, September 28th 2026
	
	
	
	
Montage Technology Announces Mass Production of Gen 5 DDR5 Register Clock Driver
Montage Technology today announced the mass production of its Gen 5 DDR5 Register Clock Driver (RCD05). Designed for high-performance DDR5 RDIMM memory modules, the RCD05 addresses the growing demand from data centers, AI servers, and other applications for memory systems with higher bandwidth and greater reliability.
Compliant with the JEDEC DDR5RCD05 specification, the RCD05 supports data rates of up to 8000 MT/s, an approximately 11% increase over the previous-generation RCD04, providing greater memory bandwidth for next-generation server platforms. The RCD05 integrates a high-performance, low-jitter PLL clock driver circuit and supports key features including continuous-time linear equalization (CTLE) and ZQ calibration, helping improve signal integrity and stability for high-speed signal transmission.
Mr. Stephen Tai, President of Montage Technology"The successful mass production of the RCD05 marks another important achievement in our continued efforts to advance DDR5 memory interface technologies. We will continue to work closely with our industry partners to deliver high-performance, highly reliable memory interface solutions that help next-generation server platforms achieve enhanced system performance."
In addition to the RCD05, Montage Technology offers a comprehensive portfolio of DDR5 RCD products supporting a range of data rates, along with memory interface and module companion chips for both server and client applications, including MRCD, MDB, CKD, SPD, PMIC, and TS. Together, these products enable Montage Technology to provide customers with a complete memory interface solution.

articles.title: Artifactory Vulnerabilities Under Active Exploitation Enable Authentication Bypass and Admin Access
articles.text:
Three Artifactory vulnerabilities under active exploitation enable authentication bypassing on Internet-accessible, self-hosted Artifactory deployments, potentially allowing attackers to establish persistent administrator access in under five minutes. The exploits can then enable dangerous post-authentication activity, including credential and key theft, arbitrary code execution, persistence, and anti-forensics measures.
Security company Wiz.io, which disclosed the three vulnerabilities, reports that attackers are chaining the flaws to achieve privilege escalation and full administrator control of self-hosted Artifactory instances:
These CVEs are trivial to exploit, a handful of unauthenticated HTTP requests. If your instance was exposed while vulnerable, assume compromise and hunt for post-exploitation artifacts. Upgrading closes the door but does not evict an attacker who is already inside [...].
The three vulnerabilities are CVE-2026-42018, rated high severity, which "may cause Artifactory to return an internal anonymous-user token to an unauthenticated requester, even when anonymous access is disabled"; CVE-2026-42016, also rated high severity, which causes Artifactory to fail to properly validate a request's token so "an attacker with low-privileged access may be able to use a valid token to perform unauthorized actions and gain elevated privileges"; and CVE-2026-82329, rated critical severity, which allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain administrative control.
As noted by Wiz.io, two of the vulnerabilities can be chained in an attack leading to persistent admin accounts and further post-exploitation.
Every exploitation followed a similar shape. An unauthenticated POST /access/api/v1/aws/token/ with a trailing slash returned HTTP 200 with a JWT for the internal anonymous user, exploiting CVE-2026-42018. The actor then exchanged that JWT for an admin-scoped token through POST /access/api/v1/tokens , which returned HTTP 200 and exploited the CVE-2026-42016 scope-validation flaw. The escalated token kept the anonymous username but carried admin authority, so later requests appear with an actor of token:anonymous.
Separately, CVE-2026-82329 can be exploited to obtain an admin-scoped token directly. Once administrative access is obtained, attackers have been observed creating persistent administrator accounts, deploying malicious Groovy plugins for code execution, harvesting credentials and Access signing keys, establishing backdoors, and deploying anti-forensics mechanisms.
Wiz also notes that, in some observed cases, attackers completed the exploitation and established administrative access in under five minutes.
Commenting on the disclosure on LinkedIn, cybersecurity specialist Erik York argued that:
Artifactory sits at the center of a LOT of software supply chains. This is exactly the kind of bug that turns into next year's SolarWinds story if it's not patched fast.
Jim Nitterauer, senior director of information security at Graylog, stressed the importance of patching all affected systems to keep supply chains safe:
Because Artifactory sits at the heart of software build pipelines, a compromise is a direct supply-chain risk and patch adoption has lagged badly, with attacks observed within four days of disclosure of the third bug.
All Artifactory self-hosted environments should be immediately patched to any version fixing the vulnerabilities, including 7.111.21, 7.117.28, 7.125.20, 7.133.29, 7.146.38, 7.161.20, or newer depending on the deployed release branch.

articles.title: Apple libera iOS 27.0.1 para corrigir bug que reinicia iPhones • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple libera iOS 27.0.1 para corrigir bug que reinicia iPhones
Atualização deve resolver falha ligada ao Face ID. Update também soluciona problemas na câmera e na tela.
A Apple liberou nesta segunda-feira (28/09) o iOS 27.0.1. A atualização deve corrigir o bug que fazia alguns iPhone 18 Pro e Pro Max travarem e reiniciarem após falha de autenticação pelo Face ID. O update começou a ser disponibilizado hoje e chega gradualmente aos usuários.
O problema foi confirmado pela empresa na semana passada. Após relatos de usuários e testes que conseguiram reproduzir as reinicializações, a Apple informou que preparava uma solução, mas não revelou a causa técnica da falha.
Segundo as notas da atualização, o iPhone 18 Pro e o 18 Pro Max podiam reiniciar inesperadamente quando o Face ID falhava ao autenticar o usuário. O problema aparecia principalmente em tentativas de acessar aplicativos ou conteúdos protegidos por biometria e o aparelho deixava de responder, reiniciando segundos depois.
O pessoal do 9to5Mac conseguiu reproduzir o erro em um iPhone 18 Pro ao tentar abrir o aplicativo Senhas com o rosto parcialmente coberto. Após a reinicialização, também foi encontrado um registro de “panic” na área de análise do sistema, indicando uma falha grave que forçou o aparelho a reiniciar. Alguns usuários chegaram a trocar seus iPhones por novas unidades por suspeitarem de um defeito de hardware.
A Apple não detalhou o que provocou as reinicializações, mas os modelos Pro desta geração chegaram no começo do mês com um Face ID repaginado.
Além da falha envolvendo o Face ID, o iOS 27.0.1 resolve outros dois problemas nos novos iPhones da linha Pro. Em algumas unidades, fotos capturadas com zoom de 2x podiam apresentar um artefato de cor em certas condições de iluminação ao usar abertura f/1.48.
A atualização corrige esse comportamento. Outro erro podia fazer a tela deixar de responder quando a Central de Notificações e a Central de Controle eram abertas ao mesmo tempo.
Os dois problemas também aparecem nas notas do iOS 27.0.1, mas a Apple não forneceu detalhes adicionais sobre a origem das falhas. Os usuários podem procurar e instalar a nova versão pelo caminho Ajustes > Geral > Atualização de Software.

articles.title: Tras cuatro años en LEGO, un trabajador recibió un regalo que prácticamente nadie puede comprar: el "ladrillo dorado"
articles.text:
Trabajar en LEGO es el sueño de mucha gente. Sobre todo de los que, como yo, tenemos el despacho lleno de sus productos. Pensar los diseños, hacerlos, darles vueltas para optimizarlos tiene que ser, al menos sobre el papel, un trabajo chulo. En cualquier caso, lo cierto es que no sabemos cómo será. Lo que sí sabemos es que acumular antigüedad en la empresa puede traer sorpresas, y si no que se lo digan al protagonista de esta historia.
Cuatro años, cuatro regalos. Todo sale de una publicación del usuario SpamMjolner en el subreddit r/lego. Por sus cuatro años en la casa como "técnico de plásticos", SpamMjolner recibió un paquete con cuatro regalos, uno por cada año de antigüedad:
- Un set LEGO Vespa 125, elegido por él mismo.
- Una pequeña figura LEGO de un Royal Life Guard (la versión danesa de la guardia real inglesa).
- Porcelana de Royal Copenhagen.
- Un ramo de flores con un ladrillo LEGO Duplo dorado escondido dentro.
Un trato excepcional. Vaya por delante que LEGO no tira la casa por la ventana con todos sus empleados. En teoría, el grupo reserva este tipo de detalles para quienes llevan bastante más tiempo en la empresa (10, 25, 40 y 50 años de antigüedad). ¿Por qué SpamMjolner se llevó un trato especial? Porque acababa de completar cuatro años de formación en un puesto muy importante para la empresa.
Un oficio muy técnico. Su puesto exige una formación específica. Es él quien se encarga de crear los ladrillos LEGO, trabajar con moldes de inyección, mantener la producción de todas las piezas de la marca y vigilar que la calidad esté a la altura. Es decir, una pericia técnica que la compañía ha querido reconocer con una pieza conmemorativa rarísima, de las que normalmente se quedan para los empleados más veteranos.
El detalle que hace salivar a los fans. En los comentarios de la publicación de Reddit hay algo que ha llamado especialmente la atención de los coleccionistas: el famoso ladrillo dorado colocado entre las flores. Los fans lo describen como una auténtica rareza, casi imposible de conseguir por otra vía que no sea la antigüedad en LEGO.
UN VISTAZO A...
Entre 100 y 200 euros. El pequeño cubito dorado, en versión Duplo, aparece de vez en cuando en webs de subastas y suele venderse por entre 100 y 200 euros. Para una pieza pequeñita de plástico cromado, no está nada mal. Y como el público no tiene forma de comprarlo, la especulación está servida.
Cuando el ladrillo era de oro de verdad. Eso sí, hubo una época en la que el premio era todavía más gordo. A finales de los años 70 y principios de los 80, LEGO recompensaba a los empleados que superaban los 25 años de antigüedad con un ladrillo 2x4 estándar de oro macizo de 14 quilates. En internet todavía quedan algunos rastros de ellos, y hablamos de un objeto de colección prácticamente incalculable.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 28, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 28, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, September 28, 2026.
Music can build bonds even as funding into Indian startups gets diverse, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Meet Sollisai Sistahs, an all-female rap crew from Tamil Nadu challenging caste and misogyny
From an eviction in Chennai to Tamil Nadu’s hip-hop scene, Sollisai Sistahs is using rap to question caste, misogyny, inequality, and the issues shaping their communities.
Funding news
Agricultural machinery company Balwaan Krishi raises Rs 100 Cr in Series B
Agricultural machinery company Balwaan Krishi has raised Rs 100 crore in Series B funding to support its next phase of growth across manufacturing, distribution and product development. The round was led by First Bridge India Growth Fund Private Equity, with participation from other institutional investors.
Arovia Consumer raises capital from Fireside Ventures
Arovia Consumer, founded by former Soulfull founder Prashant Parameswaran, has raised capital from Fireside Ventures to build a portfolio of high-potential regional packaged food brands in India. The investment is part of Fireside Ventures’ Fund IV deployments. Arovia will take significant stakes in select regional and family-owned food businesses with established consumer loyalty, physical distribution and local supply chains. It plans to identify brands across cities including Kochi, Pune, Coimbatore, Madurai, Mysuru, Mangalore, Surat and Indore. Arovia will work with promoter families to help businesses expand into new markets, channels and categories. Parameswaran previously founded Soulfull, which was acquired by Tata Consumer Products in 2021, and continued to lead the business for five years.
Other news
NSRCEL, Maruti Suzuki launch seventh mobility startup cohort
IIM Bangalore’s startup hub NSRCEL and Maruti Suzuki India have launched the seventh cohort of their Incubation Program for Mobility Startups. The six-month programme will support early-revenue to scale-stage startups working across vehicle technology, clean tech, mobility infrastructure, Industry 4.0 and 5.0, and green manufacturing. Selected startups will receive incubation support, access to paid pilot opportunities with Maruti Suzuki, industry mentoring and curated ecosystem connections. Winners can also receive a Maruti Suzuki car, international immersion opportunities and prize money.
Previous collaborations have enabled startups including EaseworkAI, Woloo, Siftly, Innovate Labs and Sand Logic to explore engagements with the automotive and mobility ecosystem. The programme seeks to help startups validate solutions in real-world environments and accelerate their transition from experimentation to commercial deployment.
Cleartrip enters holiday packages category
Cleartrip, a Flipkart company, has entered the holiday packages category by bringing flights, hotels, activities and transfers together in customisable itineraries. The new offering is part of the company’s broader strategy to evolve into a full-stack, multimodal travel platform. Unlike conventional fixed packages, Cleartrip’s model allows travellers to modify hotels, flights and activities while retaining an expert-curated itinerary.
The service also provides access to travel experts during the planning process. Once a trip is booked, travellers receive a live itinerary containing driver details, vouchers and day plans, along with 24x7 support during the journey. Cleartrip said its scale and position within the Flipkart Group enable it to negotiate pricing and inventory across travel suppliers. The company has also introduced a Price Beat Offer for eligible itineraries.
myHQ Targets Rs 100 crore revenue from Dubai
Commercial real estate marketplace myHQ is targeting Rs 100 crore in revenue from the Dubai market over its first three years of operations. The company entered the estimated ₹1,000 crore UAE market in August with a consulting-led business setup model aimed at Indian and international founders. myHQ said growing demand from Indian startups, SMEs and HNIs is driving opportunities in the region.
More than 18,400 Indian companies joined the Dubai Chamber of Commerce in 2025, while 7,579 joined during the first half of 2026. The company will offer assistance covering free-zone, mainland and offshore structures, licensing, registration, tax structuring, visas and accounting. Its three modules—Start in Dubai, Expand to Dubai and Move to Dubai—will serve businesses, founders, professionals and relocating families.
Ranbir Kapoor launches FMCG brand Flux Theory
Actor Ranbir Kapoor has entered India’s FMCG sector as Founder of Flux Theory, a new shower and body-wash brand created with Advay Jhunjhunwala and venture-building platform Think9. The brand is positioning the shower as a moment of transformation rather than a routine activity. Its first range features five body washes built around distinct personalities—Sage, Sport, Lover, Dreamer and Rebel—with different fragrances and targeted skin benefits.
The products offer benefits including hydration, cleansing, exfoliation, brightening and moisturisation. India’s bath and shower market grew 4% in value in 2025 to Rs 35,370 crore in retail sales, according to Euromonitor. Mintel research cited by the company found that 65% of Indians were not using body wash in 2024. Flux Theory plans an omnichannel presence across digital and physical retail.
FACE elects PhonePe Lending, Navi CEOs to Board
The Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment (FACE), an RBI-recognised Self-Regulatory Organisation in the fintech sector, has elected Hemant Gala, Whole-time Director and CEO of PhonePe Lending, and Rajiv Naresh, MD and CEO of Navi, as Member Directors on its Board. Gala has more than 24 years of experience across banking, payments, e-commerce and financial services, with leadership experience at ICICI Bank, Visa, HSBC and Flipkart. He was part of PhonePe’s founding team and currently leads its lending business.
Naresh has been associated with Navi since 2019 and has held several leadership positions before becoming Managing Director and CEO. Earlier, he worked as a corporate lawyer at MD&T Partners, advising Indian and international companies on private equity, venture capital, M&A, technology and telecommunications.
MagTapp rebuilds browser around AI, expands to iOS
Indian technology company MagTapp has rebuilt its browser around artificial intelligence and is expanding to iOS after recording more than six million downloads. The company, which was among the Top 8 teams in the Government of India’s Indian Web Browser Development Challenge, has integrated Alpie AI models from technology partner 169Pi into its browsing experience. MagTapp users can search for information, obtain direct answers, summarise documents, translate languages and understand difficult concepts visually without leaving a webpage.
The browser has more than 143,000 ratings and reviews, a 4.2 Play Store rating and users across 106 countries. The company plans to expand its AI capabilities and distribution, while developing a desktop browser, a larger app version and connected experiences across devices.
Snapdeal partners with YouTube for creator-led shopping
Value-focused ecommerce platform Snapdeal has partnered with YouTube as part of the YouTube Shopping affiliate programme in India. The partnership will allow eligible creators to tag and recommend Snapdeal products directly through YouTube videos, Shorts and livestreams. Creators can browse products listed on Snapdeal, tag them in their content and earn commissions on qualifying purchases. Viewers can move from product discovery to checkout while consuming content.
Snapdeal said the initiative builds on its engagement with thousands of creators across India and will create another channel for sellers and brands to reach consumers. More than 80% of Snapdeal’s orders originate from non-metro India, while most products are priced below Rs 599. The partnership is aimed at strengthening creator-led discovery and social commerce opportunities for value-conscious Indian shoppers.
Girikon.AI’s voice platform crosses 100,000 daily calls
Girikon.AI’s AI voice platform, GirikVoice, is now handling more than 100,000 calls daily, reflecting growing enterprise demand for AI-powered voice solutions. The platform can process and analyse up to one million minutes of conversations every day. GirikVoice supports inbound and outbound calls, understands customer intent, accesses relevant customer information, updates CRM records and triggers business workflows. It can also facilitate escalation to human agents when required.
The company said enterprises are increasingly moving from AI experimentation to production-scale deployments, particularly for customer interactions where context and immediacy are important. The growing volume of conversations also provides opportunities to identify recurring customer concerns, analyse sentiment and uncover operational patterns. Girikon.AI is positioning its platform as an integrated voice solution for customer engagement and business workflows.
BonV Aero supplies 45 UAVs to Indian Army
Odisha-based heavy-payload UAV startup BonV Aero has supplied 45 unmanned aerial vehicles to the Indian Army’s Eastern Command for tactical missions, including transporting critical supplies and mission-specific payloads. The deployment is aimed at supporting operations across the challenging terrain of Northeast India. The move comes as the Ministry of Defence has floated a tender for 2,715 logistics drones, highlighting the growing use of UAVs for transporting essential supplies in difficult environments.
Eastern Command operates across forested, riverine and high-altitude areas where floods, landslides, snow and steep terrain can disrupt conventional routes. BonV Aero has previously conducted drone operations and trials for the Army in locations including Tawang, Siliguri, Kargil and Nyoma, and has trained more than 150 Army personnel.
MSD appoints Vidhya Sundaram as Hyderabad Tech Centre Lead
MSD has appointed Vidhya Sundaram as Associate Vice President, Global Technology Centers and Hyderabad Tech Center Lead. Based in Hyderabad, Sundaram will oversee the company’s global Technology Center strategy and lead the Hyderabad facility as it expands its contribution to enterprise technology solutions. Her appointment follows the recent inauguration of the Tech Center’s expanded workplace in Hyderabad, which increases capacity for local teams and global collaboration. Sundaram brings more than 20 years of experience in building and scaling global capability organisations and delivering technology-driven business outcomes in the life sciences sector.
Park+ migrates core infrastructure to Akamai Cloud
Auto-tech platform Park+ has migrated its core infrastructure to Akamai Cloud in a move expected to reduce infrastructure costs by 50–60%. The migration covers more than 150 microservices running on Kubernetes, over 100 SQL databases across more than 20 clusters, and multiple Redis, Elasticsearch and Kafka clusters. It also involved transferring more than 100 TB of structured data and over 600 TB of object storage. Akamai and Park+ implemented a phased migration strategy involving parallel environments and gradual workload transfers to maintain business continuity.
Ingram Micro expands B’lore office
Ingram Micro, a technology company has announced the expansion of its Bengaluru operations with a new, larger facility. The company said the move underscores the company's continued investment in India, its second-largest market globally and also reflects its long-term commitment to the country.The expanded facility will enable Ingram Micro to expand its teams, deepen its operational capabilities, and enhance support for its partners and customers in the region.
TakeMe2Space signs launch agreement for orbital computing satellites
Hyderabad-based deeptech company TakeMe2Space has signed a Launch Service Agreement with RIDE! Space to fly two 100 kg MOI constellation satellites on the Waymaker-2 mission, targeted for late 2028 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9. The spacecraft will be the company’s first data centre-class satellites and are designed to demonstrate distributed computing in orbit. Each satellite is expected to handle about 1.5 kW of power, host 10 Nvidia Thor GPUs and 100 TB of onboard storage. Optical inter-satellite links will allow the satellites to share data and computational workloads. The mission will initially focus on Earth observation, processing imagery in orbit for near-real-time analytics and selective data downlinking, while advancing TakeMe2Space’s broader orbital data centre roadmap.
SatLeo launches India’s first dedicated commercial thermal CubeSat
SatLeo Labs has developed TAPAS-1, described as India’s first dedicated commercial CubeSat-category thermal payload and the opening flight of the country’s first full-stack commercial thermal intelligence platform. Using Thermal Infrared sensing, TAPAS-1 captures temperature information invisible to conventional optical imagery, enabling in-orbit validation of SatLeo’s thermal sensing and data-processing capabilities. The mission is expected to support applications including climate monitoring, agriculture, urban heat mapping, disaster management and infrastructure monitoring, while laying the foundation for the company’s PYRO thermal constellation. SatLeo’s technology has already been deployed on the ground. In Tumakuru, Karnataka, thermal monitoring helped track methane accumulation at a landfill and map urban heat islands, while in Ahmedabad it delivered heat forecasts and advisories for outdoor workers.
CRED announces Rs 516 crore Coin Rush rewards for members
CRED has announced the fourth edition of Coin Rush, a seven-day event running from September 29 to October 5, offering collectibles, experiences and premium products worth ₹516 crore to members. The event features more than 600 types of rewards across nearly 300 brands spanning lifestyle, travel, technology, sports and personal finance. The latest edition also introduces US stocks through Kuvera by CRED, with more than ₹2 crore in US equities available as rewards and one winner eligible to receive stocks worth ₹5 lakh. Other offerings include signed sports memorabilia, sneaker drops and CRED Originals products. Rewards will be distributed through daily jackpots, raffles, timed drops and rallies. CRED says it has 1.7 crore members.
Zelio E-Mobility seeks Rs 167.96 crore through preferential issue
Electric two- and three-wheeler manufacturer Zelio E-Mobility has received board approval to raise up to Rs 167.96 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The company plans to issue equity shares worth nearly Rs 83 crore to four non-promoter institutional and private investors, while promoters will subscribe to convertible warrants aggregating nearly Rs 85 crore. The proposed fundraise will support manufacturing expansion, distribution and development of a new three-wheeler facility in Patan, Haryana. Zelio currently operates plants in Haryana, Tamil Nadu and Odisha and has more than 400 dealers across 25-plus states. Its revenue rose 76.28% year-on-year to Rs 303.54 crore in FY2025-26.
JetSynthesys and MIXI explore India-Japan gaming partnership
Digital entertainment and technology company JetSynthesys has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Japanese digital entertainment company MIXI to explore collaboration across video gaming, esports, digital entertainment and marketing. The partnership will examine opportunities including game development and publishing support, marketing and user acquisition, esports activities, market intelligence and business development. The companies will also explore potential strategic investment opportunities. JetSynthesys said the partnership combines its understanding of India’s digital market with MIXI’s gaming and entertainment expertise. MIXI, which operates services including MONSTER STRIKE and FamilyAlbum, said India represents an important growth market for the global gaming industry. The companies intend to explore products, partnerships and experiences that can connect audiences in India and global markets.
Funding rounds drive 35% rise in employee benefits spending: Plum
Employee benefits spending at Indian startups rises 35% per employee following a funding round, according to Plum’s Standard of Employee Benefits 2026, based on more than 15,000 policies covering one million lives over four years. Startups raising Series C and later rounds recorded the biggest increase at 48%, followed by Series A companies at 40% and Series B firms at 26%. Plum said post-funding enhancements commonly include expanded healthcare coverage, parent coverage, term life and accident insurance, and maternity benefits. The share of Indian companies offering comprehensive health benefits has risen from 5% to 23% over four years. However, only 25% of funded startups offer holistic plans, compared with 43% among international companies, indicating further scope for investment in employee healthcare.

articles.title: Okta advances agentic AI security through Blueprint Alliance - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Agentic AI security pushes vendors toward shared safeguards
Agentic AI security is becoming a cross-industry challenge as autonomous systems move among products and platforms. Okta Inc. argues that building trust will require coordinated safeguards rather than isolated vendor controls.
The implications extend beyond enterprise architecture, according to Charlotte Wylie (pictured), senior vice president and deputy chief security officer at Okta. The industry also needs to communicate its approach in a way that reaches people outside security organizations and technology conferences.
“I’m hoping that some of the messaging that we’ve got out there … about how we’re steering into this bleeds well beyond the conference and well beyond the attendees here,” Wylie said. “Hopefully, they’re going back to their families and saying, ‘Hey, I know how we’re going to do this now.’”
Wylie spoke with theCUBE Research’s Krista Case and co-host Rebecca Knight at Okta’s Oktane event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed cross-industry collaboration, agentic AI security and controls for autonomous systems. (* Disclosure below.)
Blueprint Alliance connects security across platforms
The Blueprint Alliance brings Okta together with founding members, including Amazon Web Services Inc., CrowdStrike Holdings Inc., Salesforce Inc. and ServiceNow Inc. The group is working to make security controls and risk signals interoperable across agentic systems.
“Rather than trying to solve that problem alone, there is a recognition that we have to galvanize as an industry to solve this problem for our customers at a speed that they are scrambling to run after,” Wylie said. “We want to make sure that we provide an architecture, a referenceable position [for] how to use the technology that we all offer in a way that we can secure the entire agentic stack.”
That architecture must give each agent an identity, limit its permissions and provide visibility into its behavior. Together, those controls allow organizations to detect when an agent deviates from its intended purpose, according to Wylie.
“When you can scope the right permissions for an agent and you can govern those permissions effectively with products like Okta for AI Agents and you have the right visibility of how they are performing those actions … you can stop that rogue agent in its tracks,” she said. “This is, I think, how we’re trying to solve for that idea [of] how do you trust an agent in a way that you can use it effectively.”

articles.title: que se passe-t-il si le starship a un problème en orbite autour de la Terre ?
articles.text:
Une altitude de 275 kilomètres, une vitesse qui approche les 28 000 km/h, six tours de la Terre et un périple d’une dizaine d’heures. Voilà, sur le papier, ce qui était prévu pour le tout premier vol orbital du Starship. Toujours sur le papier, le vaisseau, c’est-à-dire l’étage supérieur de la fusée géante, devait amerrir calmement au large du Chili, dans l’océan Pacifique.
Mais que se passe-t-il si le lanceur s’éloigne de la partition qui devait être jouée ? Jusqu’ici, le vaisseau spatial suivait une trajectoire qui décrivait un simple arc de cercle, avec comme point final l’océan Indien. C’est le plan qui a été suivi, plus ou moins avec bonheur, lors des treize vols précédents. Mais avec le quatorzième tir, tout change.
Que se passerait-il si le Starship était en perdition pendant ses tours de la Terre ?
Pendant la retransmission du lancement diffusé par SpaceX sur X, un des commentateurs qui a animé le direct a rappelé la règle suivie jusqu’ici. Sur cette trajectoire dite « à sécurité passive », même si l’équipe perd tout contrôle, les lois de la physique garantissent que le vaisseau finira sa course dans la zone d’amerrissage de l’océan Indien :
« Nous avons effectué tous nos essais en vol selon ce qu’on appelle une trajectoire suborbitale à sécurité passive. […] Même si nous parvenons à envoyer le Starship dans l’espace et que nous perdions tout contrôle, les lois de la physique garantissent qu’il suivra une trajectoire qui le mènera à amerrir inévitablement dans cette zone de l’océan Indien, quoi qu’il arrive. »
Sauf que le vol de ce lundi devait durer près de dix heures, contre environ une heure pour les tirs suborbitaux. La sécurité passive ne joue alors plus aucun rôle. Or, un vaisseau en orbite qui ne répond plus continue de tourner autour de la Terre, jusqu’à redescendre à un endroit que personne n’a choisi.
Le problème est sérieux pour un vaisseau de 52 mètres de haut, l’étage supérieur d’une fusée qui en mesure 124 au total. SpaceX a donc prévu des filets de sécurité.
Une porte de sortie à chaque étape du vol
Premier garde-fou : le Starship a démarré sur la même trajectoire que ses prédécesseurs. « Si on ne fait rien d’autre, il redescend dans l’océan Indien », a résumé le commentateur. SpaceX avait prévu une pause d’une vingtaine de minutes avant de valider le « go » pour l’orbite, le temps pour l’équipe de vérifier l’état du vaisseau.
Sur sa page de mission, SpaceX a précisé qu’elle n’envisageait de lancer la poussée vers l’orbite qu’après s’être assurée d’avoir assez de matériel en double pour la désorbitation, c’est-à-dire le coup de frein final qui fait redescendre le vaisseau. Une alerte est pourtant survenue pendant la montée, quand l’un des six moteurs de l’étage supérieur s’est éteint plus tôt que prévu.
Dan Huot, porte-parole de SpaceX, a d’abord annoncé que le vaisseau n’irait pas en orbite, mais les contrôleurs ont fini par donner leur feu vert. Le porte-parole a ensuite précisé, dans des propos relevés par CNN, que le vaisseau n’avait plus besoin de rallumer ses moteurs conçus pour le vide pendant la mission. Vingt-cinq minutes après le décollage, un seul moteur Raptor a suffi à le placer en orbite.
Une fois en orbite, l’équipe dispose de points de contrôle répartis sur tout le vol. Ceux-ci « nous permettent d’atterrir plus tôt que prévu et d’amerrir dans une zone prédéterminée de l’océan ; de plus, des milliers de composants et de capteurs nous fournissent des données sur le Starship sur l’ensemble du véhicule », a complété le commentateur.
Plusieurs types de pannes peuvent justifier un retour anticipé à l’un de ces points : alimentation électrique, contrôle de l’orientation, réservoirs, ordinateurs de vol et capteurs de navigation. Les contrôleurs peuvent alors s’appuyer sur toute la télémétrie reçue en temps réel.
Le commentateur a enfin soulevé un paradoxe.
Le Starship est conçu pour survivre à la rentrée dans l’atmosphère, et il l’a fait « presque malgré nous », a dit le commentateur, même quand SpaceX avait retiré des tuiles de son bouclier thermique ou poussé la structure à ses limites. En juillet, le Ship 40 du 13e vol avait d’ailleurs amerri intact dans l’océan Indien, et refusait de couler.
Un vaisseau aussi solide a toutes les chances d’arriver entier en mer ou au sol : l’endroit où il redescend compte donc énormément. Le commentateur n’a pas dit autre chose : « parce qu’il est si robuste, il est extrêmement important que nous fassions tout ce qui est en notre pouvoir pour nous assurer que la rentrée s’effectue dans un endroit sûr. »

articles.title: To keep drug prices high, pharma has been piling up the patents
articles.text:
The cost of healthcare in general is a debilitating, pre-existing condition for Americans. But the high prices of prescription drugs usually stand out as a pain point. While there are many insidious reasons why Americans pay more—often far more—for their medicines than people in peer countries, exploitation of the US patent system is an obvious one.
A study published Monday in JAMA highlights just how much patent exploitation has grown since 1990. In that time, researchers found that the number of patents on small-molecule drugs has more than tripled, going from an average of 2.1 patents per drug approved in 1990 to 6.9 for those approved in 2019.
Most of the growth was in “nonprimary” patents—patents that generally aren’t related to a drug’s active ingredient, but are instead for things like minor tweaks to a drug’s nonactive ingredients, updates to the way the drug is used, or the design of specialty delivery devices, such as auto-injectors. Together, those extra patents on an individual drug can create what’s called a “patent thicket,” which delays the release of affordable generics on the market, keeping drug prices higher for longer without actual clinical advancements.
The study—led by S. Sean Tu, an expert in drug and patent law at the University of Alabama—found that the increase in patents per drug extended the time in which a drug was patented from an average of two years in 1990 to an average of 6.1 years in 2019.
“Because patent protection typically determines how long brand-name firms can charge monopoly prices, the rapid growth of nonprimary patents may contribute to limited price competition that benefits patients and the health care system by helping avoid unnecessary spending,” Tu and colleagues write.
Patent overgrowth
For the study, Tu and colleagues used publicly available data to look at small-molecule drugs approved by the Food and Drug Administration and the patents filed on those drugs. (Other types of approved drugs, like biologics, are not systematically listed by the FDA in a publicly available database.) The researchers categorized the types of patents associated with each drug and how they affected the term in which the drug remained under patent. The researchers focused on drugs granted FDA approval between 1990 to 2019, giving a five-year follow-up period for patents. Still, this likely underestimates the current sizes of patent thickets, as patent activity is now extending up to nine years after FDA approval, the authors write.

articles.title: Job-Ghosting: Professorin verrät 7 Tipps für deine Bewerbung
articles.text:
Job-Ghosting bei Berufsanfängern: Professorin gibt 7 Tipps für deine Bewerbung
„Ich bin jetzt seit einem Jahr arbeitslos und mein Fazit ist sehr ernüchternd. Ich habe 300 Bewerbungen geschrieben und bekomme kaum Rückmeldung“, beschreibt eine Jobsuchende auf Linkedin ihre derzeitige Situation. Die Lage auf dem Arbeitsmarkt ist hart, besonders für die Jobeinsteiger.
So sagt auch Jutta Rump, Professorin für Allgemeine Betriebswirtschaftslehre und Direktorin des Instituts für Beschäftigung und Employability (IBE) in Ludwigshafen: „Gerade für Young Professionals, die nach ihrer Ausbildung oder ihrem Studium die Arbeitswelt betreten, liegen die Suchzeiten im Moment zwischen neun und 15 Monaten.“ Auch die Bundesagentur für Arbeit schreibt in ihrem aktuellen Monatsbericht zur Lage am Arbeits- und Ausbildungsmarkt in Deutschland: „Die Chancen, Arbeitslosigkeit durch Aufnahme einer Beschäftigung zu beenden, sind historisch schlecht.“

articles.title: ASRock X870E Challenger Wifi Motherboard Review: A value X870E board packed with features
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The X870E Challenger sports overbuilt VRMs, flagship audio, and a slew of fast USB ports, making this inexpensive AM5 board one of the best-equipped options under $230.
Pros
- +Robust power delivery
- +Flagship-class audio codec
- +Fast USB connectivity all around
- +Flexible IO Shield
Cons
- -BIOS still needs a refresh
- -Lacks AI features
- -Slower 160 MHz Wi-Fi 7
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
The latest all-white board to land on our test bench is from ASRock. But this time, it’s more affordable than the updated X870E Taichi White we recently covered. The $230 X870E Challenger Wifi White offers a surprising number of features for the price.
Specs-wise, the Challenger comes handsomely equipped for almost any price point. Features include a flagship audio codec, robust VRMs, and ample (and fast!) USB connectivity (including USB4 ports). You also get plenty of internal storage options, with four M.2 sockets (one PCIe 5.0) and two SATA ports, and fast networking with 5 GbE and Wi-Fi 7 (160MHz). Looking at other boards at this price, some don’t include USB4, offer slower 2.5 GbE, or provide weaker audio solutions. For $230, the Challenger is a great deal for an X870E-based board, though, like everything, it has drawbacks that we’ll cover below.
On the performance front, the X870E Challenger delivered average-to-below-average results across most tests, as we again had to use our secondary DDR5-6000 kit (the Kingston kit isn’t officially supported and didn’t work after enabling the XMP/DOCP profile). Still, we’re confident it would perform a bit better if you snag some RAM on the board’s QVL list that has tighter secondary and tertiary timings.Below, we’ll examine the X870E Challenger White’s performance and other features, and see if it earns a spot on our list of the best motherboards. But before we share test results and discuss details, here are the specifications from the ASRock website:
Specifications of the ASRock X870E Challenger Wifi White
| Socket | AM5 (LGA 1718) | 
| Chipset | X870E | 
| Form Factor | ATX | 
| Voltage Regulator | 23 Phase (20x 110A SPS MOSFETs for Vcore) | 
| Video Ports | (2) USB4 (1) HDMI (v2.1) | 
| USB Ports | (2) USB 4 (40 Gbps) Type-C (5) USB 3.2 Gen 2 (10 Gbps) (3) USB 3.2 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) (2) USB 2.0 (480 Mbps) | 
| Network Jacks | (1) 5 GbE | 
| Audio Jacks | (2) Analog and SPDIF | 
| Legacy Ports/Jacks | ✗ | 
| Other Ports/Jack | ✗ | 
| PCIe x16 | (1) v5.0 (x16) (1) v3.0 (x2) | 
| PCIe x8 | ✗ | 
| PCIe x4 | ✗ | 
| PCIe x1 | (1) v3.0 (x1) | 
| CrossFire/SLI | ✗ | 
| DIMM Slots | (4) DDR5-8200+(OC), 256GB Capacity | 
| M.2 Sockets | (1) PCIe 5.0 x4 (128 Gbps) / PCIe (up to 80mm) (3) PCIe 4.0 x4 (64 Gbps) / PCIe (up to 80mm) | 
| SATA Ports | (2) SATA3 6 Gbps | 
| USB Headers | (1) USB v3.2 Gen 2x2 (20 Gbps) Type-C (2) USB v3.2 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) (2) USB v2.0 (480 Mbps) | 
| Fan/Pump Headers | (7) 4-Pin (Accepts PWM and DC) | 
| RGB Headers | (3) 3-pin ARGB Gen2 headers (1) 4-pin RGB header | 
| Diagnostics Panel | 4 LED Post Status Checker | 
| Internal Button/Switch | ✗ | 
| SATA Controllers | ✗ | 
| Ethernet Controller(s) | (1) Realtek RTL8126 5 GbE | 
| Wi-Fi / Bluetooth | Realtek 8922AE Wi-Fi 7 - 160 MHz, 6 GHz, BT 5.4 | 
| USB Controllers | ASMedia ASM4242 | 
| HD Audio Codec | Realtek ALC4082 | 
| DDL/DTS | ✗ / ✗ | 
| Warranty | 3 Years | 
Inside the Box
The retail packaging includes a few accessories to help you get up and running. You get the standard Wi-Fi antennas, two white SATA cables (one with a 90-degree connector), an installation guide, and some stickers. It’s not a lot, but par for the course in this price bracket.
Design and Features of the ASRock X870E Challenger Wifi White
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The X870E Challenger Wifi White is, as the name describes, all white. In fact, everything save for two light-gray fan headers is white, along with the onboard chips and screws that secure the M.2 heatsinks to the 8-layer, server-grade PCB. Oversized VRM heatsinks cover the top-left part of the board, with Challenger written across them.
The bottom part of the board has a DIY-friendly, toolless multi-layer heatsink for the primary M.2 socket, plus basic plate-style heatsinks with screws for the M.2 sockets and dual promontory chipset. Overall, it’s a no-frills board (no integrated RGB lighting, even), so it lacks some of the larger plate-style heatsinks and ‘EZ latch features found on more expensive boards. You’ll need an all-white build to take advantage of the all-white look, but it’s still one of the better-looking white boards, especially for its price.
Starting in the top left corner, we see two “high-density” 8-pin EPS connectors (one required) to power the processor. Surrounding those are the two “XL” heatsinks to cool the flagship-class power delivery below. To the right of the socket are four DRAM slots with locking mechanisms on both sides. ASRock lists support up to DDR5-8200, which is plenty for the platform. Our Kingston kit didn’t want to play nice with this board, which makes this the third ASRock board that doesn’t support our base test kit. As always, stick to the memory QVL list for assured support.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Above the DRAM slots are the first three (of seven) 4-pin fan headers. Each header supports PWM- or DC-controlled devices and can be tweaked through the BIOS or ASRock’s Windows-based software. The CPU_FAN1 header supports up to 1A/12W output, while the rest support up to 3A/36W each. You should have plenty of headers and enough power.
Shifting focust to the right corner and moving down, the next feature is the 4-LED POST Status Checker. There are LEDs for the CPU, Boot, VGA, and RAM. During the POST process, these light up and, if there is a problem, the offending area’s LED stays lit, giving you a general idea of where the issue is. It’s not quite as helpful as the 2-character debug display on higher-end boards, but is a lot better than nothing and typical on a lower-priced motherboard.
Continuing down the edge, we spy two (of three) 3-pin ARGB headers, just above the main 24-pin ATX power connector. ASRock’s Polychrome Sync application controls the attached RGBs, offering several canned light patterns and adjustments. Last but not least is the front panel USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 (20 Gbps) Type-C connector. If there’s one thing that stands out on this board, it’s the number and speed of the USB ports — there are a lot, and ASRock didn’t skimp on speed.
Power delivery on the X870E Challenger is one of the most robust we’ve seen, especially for a $230 budget-class motherboard. It comes with 23 total phases, 20 dedicated to Vcore. Power flows from the 8-pin EPS connectors to the Renesas RAA229628 20-phase PWM controller. From there, power heads to the more Renesas bits, this time the R2209004 110A SPS MOSFETs — a surprise to see on a board of this class. The 2,200A available will most certainly handle anything you throw at it. Flagship processors like the Ryzen 9 9950X or Ryzen 9 9950X3D2, overclocked even with extreme cooling methods, are also no problem.ALBM - board6 (bottom half):
On the bottom half of the board, we’ll start on the left where there’s a fully exposed audio solution that shows off the flagship Realtek ALC4082 codec, along with a couple of dedicated audio capacitors. While you won’t find a fancy integrated amplifier or DAC, this is the best codec for the platform and another pleasant surprise on such an inexpensive offering.
In the middle of the board are three PCIe slots. Two are full-length, and one is an open-ended x1-size slot. The top slot uses ASRock’s Reinforced Steel Slot, connects through the CPU, and is your PCIe 5.0 x16 slot (no bifurcation) for video cards. The second full-length slot at the bottom connects through the chipset and runs up to PCIe 3.0 x2, while the tiny x1 slot runs at PCIe 3.0 x1 speeds and also sources its bandwidth from the chipset. I’d like to see a PCIe 4.0 slot for extra bandwidth, but as-is it will easily support lower-bandwidth expansion needs.
Mixed among the PCIe slots, to the right of the chipset heatsink, sit four M.2 sockets. The top socket, under the large, tiered, DIY-friendly heatsink, is the one and only PCIe 5.0 x4 (128 Gbps) “Blazing” M.2 socket (M.2_1). M.2_2/3, which both run at PCIe 4.0 x4 (64 Gbps), are under the plate-style heatsink that’s secured with three captive screws. M.2_4 runs vertically along the right edge of the board and also supports PCIe 4.0 x4 drives. The good news is that the M.2 drives don't share lanes. You can pack the motherboard full of them, and each will run at full bandwidth without degrading or disabling another part. If your system needs a RAID setup on M.2, the board supports RAID0/1/10 modes. I wish there were more DIY-friendly features, but at this price, something has to give to keep prices low.
Hidden under the M.2 heatsink, along the right edge, is a 19-pin USB 3.2 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) header and the two SATA ports (supports RAID0/1 modes). Finally, we've included a few images of the board's active ICs. ASRock uses a mix of ASMedia (USB4), Realtek (audio, networking), and Renesas for the power bits.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At the bottom are several headers, including front-panel audio and USB ports. A complete list of connectivity is listed below (from L to R):
- Front panel audio
- 4-pin RGB
- 3-pin ARGB
- (2) USB 2.0 headers
- (4) 4-pin fan headers
- 19-pin USB 3.2 Gen 1 header
- 2-pin Clear CMOS jumper
- Power LED and Speaker
- Front panel
Flipping the board around to the rear IO, you can see it’s chock-full of colorful USB and other ports. On the left are Clear CMOS and BIOS Flashback buttons. Next to those are the Wi-Fi 7 (remember, it’s ‘only’ 160 MHz) antenna connections and the HDMI (v2.1) port. Next to that are stacks of colored USB ports. In total, there are 12: two USB 4 (40 Gbps) Type-C ports that double as video outputs; five USB 3.2 Gen 2 (10 Gbps), two of which are the Lightning USB ports (yellow, and designed to reduce latency by using different controllers). Three USB 3.2 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) ports (purple) support USB PD 3.0 charging up to 5V@3A (15W). Lastly, the two USB 2.0 ports are black. Above one of the Type-C ports is the Realtek 5 GbE, and finally, on the right end, is the audio stack with two 3.5mm analog jacks and SPDIF outputs.
If you’re an esports gamer where every millisecond counts, the lighting gaming ports could come in handy. Otherwise, the feature adds little value for the average user.

articles.title: SpaceX joue gros cet après-midi : la plus grosse fusée du monde tente d'atteindre l'orbite pour la première fois
articles.text:
Starship tente ce lundi 28 septembre son premier vol orbital. Le décollage est attendu à partir de 14h15, heure de Paris, depuis Starbase, au Texas, dans une fenêtre de 75 minutes. SpaceX retransmet le vol sur son site et sur X à partir de 13h40 environ (environ 35 minutes avant le lancement). Après treize vols suborbitaux, le vaisseau doit déployer 26 satellites Starlink V3 et boucler six tours de la Terre.
 Starship’s 14th flight is set to launch on Monday, Sept 28. The 75-minute launch window opens at 7:15 a.m. CT. Live coverage of the mission starts ~35 minutes before launch → https://t.co/uQKQvgaTmJ
— SpaceX (@SpaceX) September 27, 2026
Ce qui change par rapport aux treize premiers vols
Jusqu’ici, Starship montait dans l’espace avant de retomber en cloche, sans jamais faire le tour de la planète. Ses vols n’ont pas dépassé 65 minutes et se terminaient dans l’océan Indien, au large de l’Australie. Ce quatorzième vol est d’une autre nature, comme le détaille Space.com : six tours de la Terre, un peu moins de dix heures de vol et un amerrissage dans le Pacifique, à l’ouest du Chili.
Le premier étage, lui, ne change pas ses habitudes. Le Super Heavy doit retomber dans le golfe du Mexique environ sept minutes après le décollage, comme lors des vols précédents.
Une charge utile inédite, un plan de vol prudent
Le vaisseau doit emporter 26 satellites Starlink V3, les premiers exemplaires opérationnels de cette génération. Plus grands que leurs aînés, ils produisent deux fois plus d’énergie que la génération précédente. SpaceX exploite aujourd’hui environ 11 000 satellites Starlink en orbite basse.
Autre détail à retenir, rapporté par Teslarati : le vaisseau n’effectuera sa manœuvre d’insertion en orbite qu’après confirmation, par les contrôleurs au sol, qu’il reste assez de redondance matérielle pour réussir la manœuvre de sortie d’orbite en fin de mission. En clair, pas d’orbite si le retour n’est pas garanti.
Un feu vert obtenu tout récemment
Le vol, annoncé au départ pour le 22 septembre, a finalement été repoussé à ce lundi. La FAA a délivré son autorisation samedi 26 septembre, une modification de licence étant nécessaire pour un profil orbital. SpaceX avait auparavant mené, le 24 septembre, une répétition générale complète avec le booster 21 et le vaisseau 41.
 Launch rehearsal complete ahead of Starship Flight 14 pic.twitter.com/h5LBYyBqi4
— SpaceX (@SpaceX) September 24, 2026
Si le tir est repoussé
Des fermetures de la plage de Boca Chica sont prévues les 29 et 30 septembre, ce qui laisse deux dates de repli. La suite dépend du résultat : selon des documents de planification aérienne rapportés ces derniers jours, le vol 15 ne serait pas attendu avant le 19 octobre, et un premier tir depuis la Floride, sur le pas de tir LC-39A, pas avant le 30 octobre, des dates que SpaceX n’a pas confirmées. En attendant, Starship reste au cœur de ses plans et sa version d’atterrisseur lunaire doit participer en 2027 à Artemis III, une mission de test en orbite terrestre, avant le premier alunissage prévu en 2028 avec Artemis IV.

articles.title: Google adelanta el lanzamiento de sus chips de IA al espacio: para qué servirá esta tecnología
articles.text:
Alphabet llevará por primera vez sus chips de inteligencia artificial al espacio. El director ejecutivo de la compañía, Sundar Pichai, confirmó que el Proyecto Suncatcher de Google realizará su prueba inaugural en órbita, con el objetivo de evaluar si las Unidades de Procesamiento Tensor (TPU) pueden sobrevivir y funcionar fuera de la atmósfera terrestre.
El anuncio se produce meses antes de lo previsto originalmente y marca un paso concreto hacia la idea de centros de datos espaciales impulsados por energía solar.
PUBLICIDAD
Prueba espacial de las TPU de Google: en qué consiste el proyecto Suncatcher
Pichai confirmó a través de una publicación en X que las TPU se lanzarán a bordo de la próxima misión de transporte compartido Transporter-18, operada por Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX). Se trata de una iniciativa conjunta con Planet Labs PBC, que trasladará un prototipo de satélite diseñado específicamente para esta prueba.
El propio ejecutivo resumió el desafío con una frase que sintetiza el experimento: “¿Podrán nuestras TPU sobrevivir y funcionar en el espacio? Bueno, lo vamos a descubrir”, escribió Pichai en su cuenta de X.
La respuesta desde el sector aeroespacial no tardó en llegar. El director ejecutivo de SpaceX, Elon Musk, respaldó la iniciativa con dos emojis de cohetes en su respuesta a la publicación de Pichai, un gesto que reforzó la sintonía entre ambas compañías en este desarrollo.
PUBLICIDAD
Google tiene previsto lanzar el primer hardware del proyecto el 1 de octubre, a bordo de un cohete Falcon 9 de SpaceX. Esta fecha adelanta considerablemente el cronograma original, que ubicaba las pruebas para comienzos de 2027.
El satélite experimental, denominado MVP, pondrá a prueba de manera directa la visión de Google de sostener centros de datos de inteligencia artificial en órbita, un concepto que hasta ahora permanecía en fase teórica dentro de la compañía.
Capacidad técnica del satélite MVP y sus limitaciones de refrigeración
El satélite MVP incorpora cuatro TPU, con una potencia de cálculo aproximadamente equivalente a la de un servidor de centro de datos convencional. Esta comparación permite dimensionar el alcance real del experimento más allá de un simple ensayo tecnológico.
PUBLICIDAD
Uno de los mayores desafíos de operar hardware de inteligencia artificial en el espacio es la disipación del calor. Los ventiladores convencionales, utilizados en los centros de datos terrestres, no pueden funcionar en el vacío espacial, lo que obligó a Google a diseñar una solución alternativa.
Suncatcher cuenta con un sistema de refrigeración por capas pensado para gestionar el calor generado por los chips en ausencia de aire. Según explicó el ejecutivo de Google Travis Beals, los chips pueden funcionar durante unos 15 minutos antes de necesitar un período de enfriamiento.
Pese a esta limitación operativa, el satélite fue diseñado para permanecer activo durante aproximadamente un año, un período que permitirá a los equipos técnicos recopilar datos sobre el comportamiento sostenido de las TPU en condiciones orbitales.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué Google apuesta por centros de datos de IA en el espacio
Google impulsa el Proyecto Suncatcher para resolver un problema estructural del sector: el consumo energético cada vez mayor que exige el entrenamiento y funcionamiento de sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
La propuesta consiste en instalar centros de datos en órbita capaces de aprovechar la energía solar de manera directa y continua, sin las interferencias atmosféricas ni los ciclos día-noche que limitan la captación solar en la superficie terrestre.
En diciembre, Pichai ya había explicado que el proyecto busca precisamente esa eficiencia energética como respuesta a la creciente demanda de cómputo que exige la IA. En esa misma ocasión, el directivo fue más allá y planteó una proyección a mediano plazo, al sugerir que la computación orbital podría generalizarse en el transcurso de una década.
PUBLICIDAD
Musk también se había pronunciado sobre la propuesta en aquel momento, cuando calificó la iniciativa de “interesante”, un respaldo que anticipaba la colaboración que ahora se concreta con el uso de cohetes Falcon 9 y misiones de transporte compartido de SpaceX para viabilizar las primeras pruebas.
Impacto bursátil del anuncio en las acciones de Alphabet
El anuncio del Proyecto Suncatcher se produjo en un contexto de desempeño positivo para el título de Alphabet en los mercados. Según datos de Benzinga Pro, la acción GOOG acumula una suba de 8,03% en lo que va del año.
El viernes, antes de la apertura del mercado, el papel registraba un incremento adicional de aproximadamente 0,01%, hasta ubicarse en 339,06 dólares por acción, un movimiento marginal que refleja la reacción moderada de los inversores ante el anuncio del experimento espacial.

articles.title: What makes Rogers Canada's best and most reliable 5G+ network
articles.text:
Today, a phone is more than just a phone. It’s our camera, wallet, entertainment hub, navigation system, and a key connector to family and friends. When you depend on a device so heavily, reliability becomes an important differentiator.
In fact, a recent Rogers survey conducted using the Angus Reid Forum shows that reliability is the most important wireless feature for Canadian subscribers.
The best network is the one you can count on every day, which is why Rogers has once again been recognized as Canada’s best and most reliable 5G+ network by umlaut, a global leader in independent network benchmarking.
What independent testing shows
Claiming “best and most reliable” is a pretty lofty statement. But when umlaut ranks it as such, you know it’s the real deal.
Networks are evaluated by using drive testing and large-scale crowdsourced data to measure real-world customer experience. The crowdsourced data covers 99.1 per cent of the Canadian population area, while drive testing spans nearly 28,000 km across major cities, smaller communities, highways, and rural routes. All in all, a combination of the two is a pretty comprehensive dataset. Key performance indicators include coverage, speed availability, latency, and network stability.
In addition to being awarded the “Best in Test” wireless benchmark award for the eighth straight year, Rogers achieved the top scores in voice, data and reliability for wireless networks. Rogers has led on umlaut’s most reliable wireless network ranking since it was first introduced in 2021.
These results are more than a shiny acknowledgement of a job well done. They reflect how people actually use their phones every day, including voice calls, streaming, browsing, gaming, video calling, social media, and mobile productivity.
How Rogers delivers
Part of Rogers dedication to reliability is its nearly $40 billion investment in its networks over the past decade to expand coverage and improve performance. Its 5G/5G+ network combines 600 MHz low-band spectrum with 3500 MHz and 3800 MHz mid-band spectrum.
In simpler terms, low-band spectrum provides broad coverage and improved building penetration, while mid-band spectrum adds speed and capacity. Together, they deliver reliable connectivity in urban, rural, and remote areas.
We’re all familiar with the frustration of being at a concert or conference where the crowded environment means slow loading speeds. Rogers 5G+ combats this by providing additional speed and network capacity to help more people stay connected at the same time – even in high-traffic environments.
And with Priority Network Access, included in the Rogers 5G+ Ultimate plan, Canadians have priority access on the Rogers 5G+ network, giving them the fastest speeds available, even during peak times.
Beyond traditional cell coverage
Reliability is so much more than performance where cellular networks already exist. It’s also about extending connectivity beyond traditional coverage areas, such as remote locations, rural areas, and highways beyond cellular reach. In fact, traditional wireless networks only cover about 18 per cent of Canada’s vast geography.
To fill this gap, Rogers introduced Rogers Satellite, a first-of-its-kind satellite-to-mobile service in Canada where users can use text, including text-to-911 in emergencies, and satellite-ready apps like WhatsApp, Messenger, Google Maps, X, and AccuWeather outside traditional cellular coverage.
Whether you’re at a packed event or a remote campsite, the last thing you want is to find you don’t have coverage when you need it most. True reliability means helping Canadians stay connected wherever they are.
The bottom line
Reliability isn’t just a ranking. It’s a necessity. Check out Rogers 5G+ Ultimate plan, which brings together unlimited high-speed data, a five-year price guarantee, Priority Network Access and the most coverage in Canada with Rogers Satellite on one plan.

articles.title: Voice AI startup Modulate raises $25M to bring audio-native models to more developers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Voice AI startup Modulate raises $25M to bring audio-native models to more developers
Voice artificial intelligence startup Modulate Inc. today announced it has raised $25 million in new funding to get its audio-native models in front of more developers.
Modulate offers AI models that work on the raw audio of a conversation. Emotion, tone and intent all register as signals, as do signs that a voice is a deepfake. The models can combine those readings to flag a fraud attempt or a caller losing patience with a voice agent, and some of that analysis runs live while the conversation is still happening.
The company got its start moderating voice chat in online games, and harassment and child grooming on social and gaming platforms are still among the things its models look for. Health care institutions use them to screen out callers impersonating staff with deepfake voices. A newer set of customers runs voice AI agents and uses the models to check how those agents are performing.
All of that runs through Velma, Modulate’s flagship platform. Underneath it, the Ensemble Listening Model architecture picks from more than 100 small specialized audio models for each job and blends their results. Modulate says that design is up to 1,000 times more efficient than handing the same audio to one large model.
More than 10 million hours of audio a month now run through the models, Modulate said, and the lifetime total recently passed 600 million hours. Two of its products have also taken first place on Hugging Face leaderboards this year. The transcription model topped the Open ASR Leaderboard in July, and Velma Deepfake Detect, which launched in March, sits at the top of the Speech Deepfake Arena. The company said the deepfake model is 98.9% accurate on public benchmark data.
“Voice is becoming a primary interface for AI, and that creates a whole new set of problems that can’t be solved from a transcript,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Carter Huffman.
Huffman said developers “shouldn’t have to rebuild the audio intelligence layer every time they create a new voice experience,” and part of the funding goes toward reaching them. New software development kits and application programming interfaces are in the works, as are models built for specific industries.
Hiring will pick up in research, engineering and developer relations, and the company is building out partner integrations and more ways for customers to deploy its models. Developers can already buy batch transcription through its existing API for three cents an hour.
Future Ventures led the round, with participation from returning investors Hyperplane and Lakestar. Hyperplane backed Modulate’s $2 million seed round, and Lakestar led its $30 million Series A in 2022. Steve Jurvetson, a co-founder of Future Ventures, said Modulate has “gained a significant technical lead in audio-native AI” and that the need for its technology is spreading well beyond where it started, into AI agents and security.
Huffman and fellow co-founder Mike Pappas are both Massachusetts Institute of Technology alumni and started the company in 2017. Counting the new round, backers have put $60 million into Modulate.

articles.title: Google acaba com o Gemini Gems e anuncia migração para nova ferramenta • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google acaba com o Gemini Gems e anuncia migração para nova ferramenta
Ferramenta será encerrada em novembro e dará lugar ao sistema de Habilidades introduzido com o Gemini Spark.
O Google decidiu acabar com a função do Gemini que permite criar versões personalizadas de inteligência artificial, chamada de Gemini Gems. As configurações serão migradas para o novo sistema de habilidades do Gemini Spark a partir de 17 de novembro.
Um aviso dentro da plataforma informa a data de encerramento e explica que os Gems continuarão funcionando normalmente até que o recurso seja substituído.
O Google, porém, ainda não explicou como ficará o acesso às habilidades para quem utiliza a versão gratuita do Gemini. Os ajustes de habilidades, atualmente, são disponíveis apenas para assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro ou Ultra através da aba Spark.
A mudança faz parte de uma reorganização dos recursos de personalização do Gemini. Antes da confirmação oficial, referências encontradas no código dos aplicativos do Google já haviam indicado que a empresa trabalhava na substituição ou integração dos Gems com o novo sistema, segundo o site Android Authority.
Os Gems eram uma forma de personalizar o Gemini para que ele seguisse um conjunto de instruções. A funcionalidade era direcionada a quem precisa usar sempre as mesmas regras, evitando a repetição das preferências durante a conversa.
Dessa forma, era possível criar um Gem para finalidades específicas, como estudos, escrita ou outras instruções. O usuário definia essas orientações durante a criação e, depois, podia recorrer à versão personalizada do Gemini quando quisesse realizar aquela atividade.
As habilidades são o novo formato do Google para personalizar o comportamento do Gemini e levam a ideia do Gems para um modelo mais integrado aos fluxos de trabalho. Segundo o Google, assim como os Gems, elas indicam como uma determinada tarefa deve ser realizada.
A principal diferença é a integração às capacidades do Gemini Spark, que é um assistente voltado a automatização de processos. A IA pode, por exemplo, identificar automaticamente quando uma atividade é relevante e aplicá-la em segundo plano.
Também é possível combinar várias habilidades na mesma tarefa. Uma pode, por exemplo, definir como uma reserva de viagem deve ser organizada, enquanto outra determina como o Gemini deve preparar uma mensagem no Gmail.
