articles.title: El cohete más grande jamás construido acaba de alcanzar la órbita: Starship ha cruzado una de sus grandes fronteras
articles.text:
Starship no se parece demasiado a la imagen tradicional que tenemos de un cohete. Es una enorme mole de acero inoxidable de 124 metros de altura que SpaceX ha lanzado una y otra vez para probar, vuelo tras vuelo, cómo separar sus etapas, regresar desde el espacio y recuperar un sistema concebido para ser reutilizado. Hemos visto avances enormes y también vehículos perderse por el camino, pero todo ese desarrollo seguía teniendo una ausencia llamativa: la etapa superior nunca había llegado a quedarse en órbita. Esa barrera acaba de caer.
El vuelo número 14 ha llevado por fin a la Ship 41 hasta donde SpaceX quería verla. Tras despegar desde Starbase sobre el Super Heavy y separarse después del enorme propulsor, la etapa superior continuó su ascenso y realizó unos 25 minutos más tarde el encendido necesario para entrar en órbita terrestre. Desde allí ha desplegado los 26 Starlink V3 transportados en su bodega, una carga que, a diferencia de la utilizada en el vuelo anterior, permanecerá en órbita para iniciar el proceso de incorporación a la constelación.
Starship ya está "dando vueltas" en la órbita
Hubo un momento, sin embargo, en el que esa entrada en órbita estuvo en riesgo. Uno de los tres Raptor Vacuum de la etapa superior se apagó antes de tiempo durante el ascenso y el propio portavoz de SpaceX, Dan Huot, llegó a anunciar durante la retransmisión que no se intentaría la maniobra orbital. La decisión no fue definitiva. Los equipos comprobaron después que los tres motores centrales seguían funcionando correctamente y mantenían la redundancia necesaria para ejecutar la inserción y el posterior desorbitado. Pocos minutos más tarde autorizaron el encendido que permitió continuar con el plan.
La diferencia con los vuelos anteriores no está simplemente en haber llegado más alto. Hasta ahora, Starship seguía trayectorias suborbitales: alcanzaba el espacio, pero su recorrido estaba diseñado para terminar de nuevo en la Tierra sin quedar en órbita alrededor del planeta. Esta vez la Ship 41 adquirió la velocidad y la trayectoria necesarias para permanecer dando vueltas a la Tierra. SpaceX había planteado inicialmente unas seis órbitas durante casi diez horas, aunque durante el vuelo actualizó ese plan y anunció que desorbitaría el vehículo después de tres horas, sin precisar el motivo del cambio.
Los 26 Starlink V3 ayudan a entender por qué esta misión va bastante más allá de demostrar que el sistema puede mantenerse alrededor del planeta. En el vuelo anterior, la etapa superior ya había desplegado unidades de esta generación, pero aquellas siguieron una trayectoria suborbital y terminaron reentrando poco después. Esta vez los satélites han quedado en órbita y están destinados a incorporarse a la constelación tras elevar su órbita. SpaceX asegura además que cada V3 está diseñado para ofrecer aproximadamente diez veces más capacidad de bajada y 22 veces más de subida que los V2, un salto que explica por qué Starship será importante para ampliar la red.
Entre esos 26 satélites hay tres que, antes de centrarse en su trabajo dentro de la constelación, mirarán hacia atrás. Sus cámaras están preparadas para fotografiar el escudo térmico de la Ship 41 desde el exterior y enviar ese material a SpaceX, que sigue intentando entender cómo responde la protección de la nave después de cada vuelo. Esta misión incorpora además cambios en la sujeción y el diseño de algunas losetas, junto con dos piezas reutilizadas de la Ship 40. Son pruebas pequeñas dentro de un problema mucho mayor: conseguir que la etapa superior pueda regresar y volar de nuevo con cada vez menos intervención.
El Super Heavy tuvo sus propios problemas, independientes de lo ocurrido después con la nave. Cuando el propulsor inició la maniobra de regreso, solo 31 de sus 33 motores volvieron a encenderse para el boost-back burn, y durante el ascenso uno de ellos ya había parecido apagarse antes de tiempo. Eso no impidió que completara la secuencia prevista hacia el mar: SpaceX confirmó su amerizaje frente a Starbase, aunque en ese momento todavía no estaba claro si el descenso había terminado con la suavidad que buscaba la compañía.
Todo esto tiene además una lectura que conduce hacia la Luna. La NASA ha contratado a SpaceX para desarrollar Starship HLS, una variante destinada a funcionar como módulo de alunizaje dentro de Artemis, pero llegar a órbita es solo una de las capacidades necesarias para ese futuro. Artemis III probará en 2027, desde la órbita terrestre, operaciones entre Orion y uno o ambos vehículos de prueba de los módulos comerciales desarrollados por SpaceX y Blue Origin. El primer alunizaje tripulado del programa está ahora previsto para Artemis IV, en 2028, mientras Starship todavía debe resolver varios desafíos.

articles.title: OpenAI teams up with Sachin Tendulkar to demystify AI in India
articles.text:
OpenAI teams up with Sachin Tendulkar to demystify AI in India
Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has teamed up with OpenAI in a multi-year partnership to show how ChatGPT can be used for everyday learning, idea generation, and personal interests.
Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has officially joined forces with OpenAI in a multi-year partnership designed to demystify artificial intelligence and show everyday users across India how ChatGPT fits into real life.
The collaboration aims to make advanced tech approachable by highlighting practical, relatable use cases.
“Much of my learning starts with a question. With ChatGPT, I can keep asking, build on an idea, and explore something at my own pace—whether I’m preparing for a speech or learning about something I enjoy. I hope that gives more people a starting point to try it for themselves with something they care about,” says Sachin Tendulkar.
The campaign posted on the platform X kicks off with a playful video where Tendulkar challenges ChatGPT to guess his identity within ten questions. Future rollouts will feature interactive content, experiential campaigns, and creator collaborations—including videos alongside tech entrepreneur Varun Mayya.
According to Prabhjeet Singh, Managing Director for OpenAI India, connecting with a figure who resonates across generations helps bridge the gap between technology and trust. The partnership comes at a period of surging AI adoption across the country. OpenAI revealed that ChatGPT’s user base in India has doubled over the past year, with most users leveraging the tool for education, writing, and everyday problem-solving.

articles.title: Decathlon baisse le prix de son home-trainer connecté le moins cher, le Van Rysel D100 Edition — Frandroid
articles.text:
Un home-trainer connecté permet de pédaler au sec pendant que la pluie tombe dehors. Mais les modèles haut de gamme comme le Garmin Tacx Neo 3M ou le Wahoo Kickr Move dépassent vite les mille euros. Decathlon, lui, propose avec sa marque Van Rysel le D100, un modèle à transmission directe vendu à petit prix et livré d’origine avec le pignon Zwift Cog et la commande Zwift Click. Une excellente porte d’entrée vers le cyclisme virtuel qui devient encore plus abordable, puisque son prix chute sous les 250 euros.

- Une transmission directe silencieuse
- Le Zwift Cog et la commande Zwift Click inclus d’origine
- Jusqu’à 600 watts de puissance et 6 % de pente simulée
Vendu habituellement 269 euros dans cette version Zwift Edition (il était sorti à 300 euros en octobre 2024), le Van Rysel D100 perd 20 euros sur le site de Decathlon et tombe à 249 euros.

Zwift Cog et Click, le duo qui change l’entraînement

articles.title: Android Auto 17.8 est là : la nouvelle mise à jour cache l'IA que Google prépare pour votre voiture
articles.text:
Android Auto 17.8 est là : la nouvelle mise à jour cache l'IA que Google prépare pour votre voiture
Google déploie la version stable d'Android Auto 17.8 sans la moindre nouveauté apparente. Son code dévoile pourtant les fondations de Magic Cue, l'assistant proactif des Pixel, tandis que les barres de réseau refont surface chez certains conducteurs.
Aucune fanfare, aucun nouvel écran d'accueil. Google a promu la version 17.8 d'Android Auto sur le canal stable une semaine à peine après la bêta 17.8.1638. Le paquet, estampillé 17.8.6638, a surgi sur APKMirror le 25 septembre au soir, avant que le site spécialisé autoevolution ne confirme le déploiement deux jours plus tard. La diffusion s'opère par vagues successives : patience, donc, si la mise à jour boude encore votre téléphone.
La note de version tient en une ligne, fidèle à une habitude tenace de la firme de Mountain View.
Magic Cue et widgets : ce que cache le code d'Android Auto 17.8
Il faut plonger dans les entrailles de l'application pour saisir la portée de ce cru. Les analystes d'AndroidSage y ont débusqué un paramètre baptisé settings_magic_cue_enabled_default. Derrière ce nom cryptique se profile Magic Cue, l'assistant maison des Pixel, qui croise Gmail, Agenda, Keep ou Messages pour suggérer la bonne information au bon moment. Google en avait esquissé la déclinaison automobile en mai, en montrant l'envoi d'une adresse depuis une simple notification de message.
Autres indices : un réglage consacré aux widgets affichés en marge du guidage, et l'import complet de la palette Material 3 Expressive. Deux briques de la refonte dévoilée le 12 mai lors de l'Android Show, encore inactives.
Barres de réseau et raton laveur : ce qui change déjà
Plusieurs conducteurs voient réapparaître l'indicateur de réseau cellulaire, volatilisé depuis des mois sans explication. Google n'a jamais officialisé ce correctif et les témoignages demeurent épars.
Jimothy, le raton laveur devenu viral cet été et tapi dans le code de la version 17.6 en mascotte météo, a en revanche quitté le navire.
Depuis le 22 septembre, les adeptes de pauses ludiques profitent par ailleurs d'une trentaine de jeux sortis de bêta, jouables uniquement véhicule à l'arrêt. Les plus pressés installeront l'APK autonome ; les autres attendront sagement leur tour sur le Play Store.

articles.title: The latest Microsoft Office 2024 Professional Plus suite is $39 in this limited-time deal
articles.text:
Microsoft Office has been the backbone of productivity for decades, and Office 2024 continues that legacy with a cleaner design, new features, and performance upgrades.
For a limited time, you can pick up a lifetime license for Microsoft's latest release, Office 2024 Professional Plus, for just $39 using coupon code TECHSPOT15. It's a one-time purchase that includes Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and Access, with no recurring fees attached.
What's New in Office 2024?
Microsoft Word gets a set of quality-of-life upgrades aimed at long documents and collaboration. There's improved Document Recovery, full support for ODF 1.4, and a long-overdue option to clear all resolved comments in a single click. New collaboration tools make it easier to share documents, leave inline comments, ask questions directly in the file, and switch between Viewing, Reviewing, and Editing modes without friction.
Transferring images from your phone to your PC used to be a multi-step process, but with Office 2024, you can now seamlessly insert photos directly from your device into your documents.
Microsoft Excel continues its steady evolution with better performance and more flexible formulas. Dynamic arrays are now more deeply integrated, allowing formulas to return multiple values that automatically expand as new data is added. New text and array functions make complex data manipulation easier, particularly for users working with large datasets or advanced formulas.
The new Outlook focuses on reliability and usability rather than flashy changes. Microsoft has improved search, refined calendar and mail syncing, and enhanced accessibility features like better screen reader support and more consistent keyboard navigation. Offline functionality has also been tightened up, making it easier to manage email and calendars even when you're not connected.
Access is the key addition in the Professional Plus edition. Microsoft's database application lets users build custom data management tools, create forms and reports, track inventory, manage customer records, and automate workflows without requiring a full-scale database server. While many users may never need it, Access remains useful for small businesses and power users who work with structured data.
Microsoft PowerPoint's updates are especially useful for hybrid work. You can now record presentations that capture your voice, ink annotations, and even on-camera video, then export everything as a shareable video file. Accessibility gets a boost too, with easier tools for adding closed captions to both audio and video content.
Lifetime license details
Office 2024 Professional Plus largely builds on the foundation of Office 2021, but it ships with a refreshed default theme inspired by Windows 11's Fluent Design system. Microsoft has also introduced a new default font, Aptos, replacing Calibri to give documents a more modern, readable look.
Microsoft describes Office 2024 as a "locked-in-time" release, a deliberate alternative to the constantly changing Microsoft 365 apps. It's aimed at users who prefer stability over a steady stream of feature updates and don't want to pay a subscription just to keep using Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, or Access.
The company has committed to five years of official support, including security updates and bug fixes, running through October 10, 2029. This deal includes instant delivery of your license key and download, so you can install and activate Office 2024 immediately: no waiting, no subscriptions, and no recurring charges.

- Windows 11 Pro available for $10
- Microsoft Office 2021 Pro available for $29
- Microsoft Project 2021 for Windows for $15
- Microsoft Visio 2021 for Windows for $15
- Microsoft Visual Studio Pro 2026 for $35

articles.title: Lenovo Introduces Its First Googlebook, Delivering Premium AI Experiences in a Sleek, Lightweight Design
articles.text:
Monday, September 28th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Lenovo Introduces Its First Googlebook, Delivering Premium AI Experiences in a Sleek, Lightweight Design
Lenovo today introduced the Lenovo Googlebook 15, its first Googlebook, expanding the company's laptop portfolio by combining Google's computing experiences with Lenovo's signature design, engineering, and user-focused innovation. Powered by Intel Core Ultra 5 processors with built-in Gemini Intelligence, up to 32 GB of memory and up to 512 GB of storage, the Lenovo Googlebook 15 helps users stay productive and connected - no matter where the day takes them.
Designed for professionals, creators and business owners, the Lenovo Googlebook 15 delivers up to 47 TOPS of performance while weighing under 3 lbs., making it the lightest 15-inch device in Lenovo's portfolio.
Benny Zhang, Executive Director and General Manager of Chromebooks in Lenovo's Intelligent Devices Group"The Lenovo Googlebook 15 represents the next step in Lenovo's collaboration with Google and our commitment to making powerful intelligent experiences accessible to more people," "By combining Google's intelligence capabilities with Lenovo's expertise in bringing devices to life through thoughtful design and engineering, we are expanding our portfolio with a new option designed for today's connected lifestyles."
See Every Detail - Feel Every Moment
The Lenovo Googlebook 15 features a stunning 15-inch 2.8K OLED touchscreen display with a 120 Hz refresh rate and 100% DCI-P3 color coverage, making everything from creative projects to everyday browsing look sharper and more vibrant.
A responsive haptic touchpad provides precise tactile feedback for smoother navigation, while the quad-speaker system with Dolby Atmos delivers rich, room-filling audio for music, movies, and video calls. Support for intuitive pinch, zoom, and precision scrolling further enhances the premium, immersive user experience.
Lightweight by Design. Built to Last.
With its lightweight design, durability to help withstand everyday bumps and wear, and up to 12.5 hours of battery life, the Lenovo Googlebook 15 combines portability with resilience, giving users the freedom to move seamlessly between work, creativity, and downtime.
Thoughtful design details elevate the experience even further. The signature Glowbar lets users check battery and charging status, even when the lid is closed, while a premium anti-fingerprint-coated metal chassis feels smooth to the touch. An integrated fingerprint reader and facial authentication enable fast, protected sign-in, and a built-in camera shutter gives users added privacy.
Smarter Productivity, Built In
Gemini Intelligence helps individuals get from idea to action in seconds. With Magic Pointer, the cursor just got its first glow-up in years to let individuals do more than simply point and click. Wiggle the cursor to activate Gemini and turn two images into a poster or add a date to the calendar instantly. The Lenovo Googlebook 15 also stays seamlessly in sync with Android devices, making it easy to switch between devices and access apps and files directly from a connected phone.
With Rambler, voice-to-text becomes smarter and more natural. Users can press the dictation key on their Googlebook to automatically remove filler words and add formatting, transforming their stream of consciousness into polished text. Whether brainstorming ideas, drafting emails, or coding, users can speak naturally while Rambler keeps up, even when they switch languages mid-sentence.
The device also includes 12 months of Google AI Pro, giving users expanded access to powerful features in the Gemini App, 5 TB of cloud storage to keep photos and files backed up, and subscriptions to apps like Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, and CapCut.
Designed specifically for Googlebook, Lenovo AI Mouse makes everyday AI interactions faster and more intuitive. Users can instantly access Gemini with a click, launch contextual actions with Magic Pointer, and personalize controls to fit the way they work.
By combining Google's latest software and AI capabilities with thoughtful design, premium audiovisual experiences, and all-day productivity, the Lenovo Googlebook 15 delivers a smarter, more intuitive computing experience that adapts to the way people work, create, learn, and stay connected.

The Lenovo Googlebook 15 will be available starting October 4th, 2026 starting at $1,099.99.

articles.title: Meta’s ZGateway Cuts ZippyDB Connections 19x While Handling 1B+ Operations per Second
articles.text:
Meta introduced ZGateway, a stateless proxy layer for ZippyDB, its widely used distributed key-value store, to address connection and reliability challenges created by more than one million client hosts. The gateway handles more than 1 billion operations per second and about 40% of ZippyDB traffic, while Meta’s model estimates that the architecture reduces total persistent connections by roughly 19x.
ZippyDB direct access versus ZGateway architecture (Source: Meta Blog Post)
ZippyDB supports product metadata, counters, configuration and other workloads across Meta’s globally distributed infrastructure. In the direct access model, clients connect to the database hosts serving the shards they access. A single client can touch tens of thousands of shards distributed across hundreds of thousands of database hosts, creating a dense many-to-many connection mesh. Meta said connection storms could contribute to file descriptor exhaustion and out-of-memory conditions.
ZGateway places a managed proxy tier between clients and ZippyDB servers. Clients maintain sticky connections to regional gateway hosts, while database servers receive connections from the controlled gateway fleet. ZGateway runs as regional tiers discovered through ServiceRouter, Meta’s hyperscale service mesh solution, keeping clients near their gateway. The gateway uses Meta’s existing C++ ZippyDB client as its request engine and supports both a pure proxy and read-through cache tier. Meta’s model estimates that per-host connection counts fall by approximately 97 to 98%, while total persistent connections decline by roughly 19x.
The change also shifts where shared traffic management occurs. ZGateway can authenticate and authorize requests, apply per-tenant admission control, resolve shards, use local caching, and batch or coalesce requests before forwarding them to ZServer replicas. Because the gateway sees traffic from multiple clients, it can combine requests that individual client libraries cannot observe across processes.
ZGateway request path from client through regional gateway to ZServer replicas (Source: Meta Blog Post)
The proxy pattern is also used in connection poolers, service meshes, CDNs, and API gateways, although their responsibilities and scaling tradeoffs differ. Meta’s earlier description of ZippyDB shows that the database itself already provides managed sharding, replication, failure detection, and capacity management, while ZGateway adds a shared traffic management layer in front of those capabilities.
The additional network hop is a deliberate tradeoff. Md Shuvo, an architect at Sherbrook, highlighted the point in a LinkedIn post:
Adding an extra network hop actually improves overall latency by freeing up database nodes from the brutal overhead of connection management.
ZGateway also provides a centralized location for load balancing, cross-region resilience, caching, and overload protection. In a controlled test above 90% CPU, six of approximately 1,350 tenant buckets shed traffic while the remaining tenants processed 99.9% of requests without rejection. Meta can progressively route traffic by service, shard prefix, percentage, or region, with a global kill switch for rollback.
Meta plans to route all ZippyDB traffic through ZGateway while exploring agent-operated controls, selective co-location with ZServer, and a multi-process architecture for stronger fault isolation.

articles.title: Kalshi loses again as judges rule prediction markets must obey gambling laws
articles.text:
Another federal appeals court has ruled that states can enforce their gambling laws against the prediction market Kalshi, which asserts that it can only be regulated by the US government. On Friday, a three-judge panel in the US Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit ruled unanimously against Kalshi and in favor of Ohio and Tennessee.
While the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission has exclusive jurisdiction over “swaps,” the judges found that sports wagers offered on Kalshi do not meet the legal definition of swaps. Moreover, the court found that even if Kalshi wagers were swaps, the regulatory scheme created by Congress would not prohibit states from enforcing gambling laws on prediction markets.
“We hold that Kalshi has not shown that its sports-event contracts satisfy the statutory definition of a ‘swap’ so as to fall within the scope of the CFTC’s ‘exclusive jurisdiction,’” said the ruling written by Judge Julia Smith Gibbons, a George W. Bush appointee. “And, even assuming that Kalshi’s sports-event contracts are swaps, we alternatively hold that the CEA [Commodity Exchange Act] neither expressly nor impliedly preempts Ohio’s or Tennessee’s gambling laws.”
Kalshi sued Ohio and Tennessee after gambling regulators in each state indicated they would bring enforcement actions against the prediction market. The appeals court ruling on Friday upheld an Ohio district court decision against Kalshi and vacated a Tennessee district court order that went in favor of Kalshi.
Many states are trying to stop or restrict gambling on Kalshi, which offers sports betting throughout the US despite not obtaining state gambling licenses or paying state gambling taxes. Kalshi offers sports bets in some states where gambling on sports is entirely illegal and in other states where the law has restrictions on betting that Kalshi does not follow.

articles.title: Why investors should pay attention to digital movements | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Some of the most useful signals for investors appear at the edges of established categories. Digital movements are one of those places.
They are unusually demanding forms of online community. They need to attract attention, build trust, turn that attention into participation, coordinate people and, in many cases, mobilise financial support. Many of those behaviours (direct relationships, community building, recurring participation and financial support) are already familiar from the creator economy. What is interesting is seeing the same dynamics emerge around people whose primary purpose is a cause rather than content.
That makes digital movements useful to study well beyond activism itself. They offer investors a particularly visible example of how community-driven behaviour is changing.
Fragmentation reveals what users actually want
A movement may start on Instagram, collect signatures somewhere else, coordinate its most active supporters on WhatsApp, receive financial backing through another provider and manage contacts in a spreadsheet or CRM.
The obvious observation is that the toolset is fragmented. The more interesting one is what movement leaders are trying to do across those tools: manage one continuous relationship with their community. In practice, that means fewer handoffs between discovery, participation, communication, payments and ongoing engagement.
What many organisers want is not five different products solving five separate parts of the journey, but a single environment where they can build, activate and sustain their community over time.
For investors, the signal is broader than the tools themselves. When users repeatedly combine several products to create what they experience as one workflow, it means behaviour has moved faster than the products serving it.
The demand is moving online
The relationship between people and the causes they care about is also becoming more digital. Discovery, participation and financial support are increasingly taking place in the same environment where younger generations already manage much of their lives.
A 2026 study by Simon-Kucher and UNICEF Germany found that 39% of young people use digital formats. Give.org has similarly found that 82% of Gen Z and Millennials use giving platforms often or sometimes when deciding where to direct their financial support.
The point is not that every form of support will become digital, but that a large existing behaviour is changing channels. And expectations move with it. Causes also tend to carry a level of emotional commitment that is very different from a purely transactional relationship.
When people feel personally connected to an issue, that relationship can translate into deeper participation and, in most cases, significantly greater financial support over time. In the aforementioned study, Give.org also found that 49% of giving-platform users prefer feeling connected to the organisation they support and receiving updates rather than avoiding follow-up contact.
For investors, the implication is that acquisition alone may tell less of the story. As relationships become more digital and persistent, the ability to retain people, re-engage them and deepen participation becomes a more meaningful signal of value.
Reach is becoming the easy part
Social platforms have dramatically lowered the barriers to reaching people. A doctor, scientist, activist or ordinary citizen can now find an audience around an issue without first building a large institution. But reach and organisation are different things.
A campaign can attract thousands of views, followers or signatures and still fail to create a community capable of acting again. Digital movements offer an unusually clear version of a challenge that also exists in creator businesses and community-led products: acquisition is visible; continuity is harder to measure.
For investors, this should raise questions about the metrics used to evaluate community-driven products. Member count and reach describe the top of the funnel. Repeated participation, direct relationships and the ability of members to bring others in say much more about whether a community is becoming durable.
Small teams are gaining organisational capacity
Another shift is happening on the supply side. Digital tools are allowing individuals and very small teams to operate with a level of organisational capacity that was once available mainly to established organisations.
AI could make that shift more significant. Research, content production and supporter communication once required organisational capacity that an individual or tiny team simply did not have. Increasingly, software can provide some of that capacity.
That does not just make existing organisations more efficient. It allows more individuals to build communities, communicate at scale and organise people around an objective at a level that was previously out of reach.
For investors, this matters because it expands the number of people capable of building direct relationships with communities at scale, a behaviour already familiar from the creator economy: building trust, gathering a community and developing a direct relationship with the people who choose to support what they do.
Why movements are worth watching
Fragmented user journeys, direct relationships, recurring participation, digital financial support and smaller operating teams are all dynamics that already matter across the creator economy and other community-driven products.
Digital movements make them unusually visible because the stakes of participation are higher. Attention without action achieves little. Participation without continuity disappears quickly. And a large audience that cannot coordinate is less powerful than a smaller community that can.
That is why digital movements are worth watching from an investment perspective. They may be one of the clearest examples of creator-economy behaviours expanding beyond entertainment and content into communities organised around shared causes and objectives.
For investors, digital movements offer a useful reminder that the value of an online community is not captured by how many people it can reach once, but by how effectively it can turn that attention into sustained participation. That is a question worth asking far beyond activism.

articles.title: Apple perde disputa de R$ 30 bilhões por patentes • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple perde disputa de R$ 30 bilhões por patentes
Taction Technology alega que iPhones e Apple Watches usam tecnologia háptica sem licença. Apple contesta decisão.
Um júri federal de San Diego, nos Estados Unidos, concluiu que a Apple violou duas patentes de tecnologia háptica pertencentes à Taction Technology e fixou mais de US$ 5,7 bilhões em indenização, quase R$ 30 bilhões em conversão direta. A disputa envolve o Taptic Engine, componente usado em iPhones e Apple Watches para produzir vibrações e respostas táteis em interações com os aparelhos.
A Apple discorda do resultado e dos danos estabelecidos e afirmou que pretende recorrer. Os jurados também concluíram que a violação não foi intencional.
A Taction processou a Apple em 2021, alegando que versões do Taptic Engine usadas em iPhones e Apple Watches incorporavam tecnologias protegidas pelas patentes americanas 10.659.885 e 10.820.117 sem uma licença adequada. O documento do processo cita mecanismos destinados a produzir vibrações táteis com maior controle sobre frequências e ressonâncias.
As duas patentes envolvem tecnologias que transformam sinais elétricos em movimentos que podem ser sentidos pelo usuário e utilizam elementos como bobinas e ímãs para reduzir vibrações indesejadas e controlar a resposta do mecanismo. Na prática, esse tipo de resposta permite que um celular ou relógio simule sensações como o clique de um botão ou produza diferentes padrões de vibração para alertas e comandos.
A empresa sustentou que versões mais recentes do Taptic Engine usam estruturas semelhantes às descritas em suas patentes e também citou o iPhone SE de 2020 como um dos exemplos de aparelhos que incluíam componentes contestados. O júri concluiu que a Apple infringiu as duas patentes, mas considerou que a violação não foi intencional.
A dona do iPhone contesta tanto a conclusão de violação quanto o valor da indenização. Em declaração divulgada após o veredito, a empresa afirmou que o Taptic Engine é “fundamentalmente diferente” da tecnologia da Taction e que não utiliza a tecnologia da rival. Não há até agora determinação para interromper a venda de iPhones ou Apple Watches e a indenização bilionária pode mudar durante recursos e outras etapas do processo.
A disputa, no entanto, já passou por outras reviravoltas. A ação foi aberta em 2021, e a Apple obteve uma decisão favorável em 2023. Posteriormente, o Tribunal de Apelações do Circuito Federal reverteu parte da decisão e determinou que o caso voltasse a julgamento. O novo julgamento começou em 14 de setembro e terminou com a decisão desta semana.
O caso se soma a outras discussões envolvendo patentes em produtos da Apple. Nos Estados Unidos, a companhia chegou a desativar o sensor de oxigênio de alguns Apple Watches durante uma disputa separada com a fabricante de equipamentos médicos Masimo.

articles.title: Physical AI custom chip startup SiMa.ai raises $150M at $1.45B valuation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Physical AI custom chip startup SiMa.ai raises $150M at $1.45B valuation
Custom physical artificial intelligence chip startup SiMa.ai Technologies Inc. today announced it has raised $150 million in new funding at a $1.45 billion valuation to scale up its development environment and fund the next generation of its embedded AI compute platform.
Physical AI devices are hardware systems including robots, drones and autonomous vehicles that integrate artificial intelligence with sensors and actuators to reason about and take action in relation to the real world. The iconic example is a self-driving car that uses AI to “see” the world using cameras and laser imaging, stop at stoplights and work within traffic.
The global market for physical AI devices continues to surge as more connected machines are transformed into intelligent interfaces and SiMa.ai is building the hardware and software that will act as the “brains” for these machines.
“Physical AI in humanoids, automotive, and drones is the gateway to a $50 trillion market that has remained largely untouched by modern innovation,” said founder and Chief Executive Krishna Rangasayee. “While others are still figuring out the pieces or repurposing their cloud offerings, we’ve built the entire puzzle.”
Fidelity Management & Research Company and Amplify co-led the Series C financing round. Alter Venture Partners, Dell Technologies Capital and StepStone Group also participated in the round, alongside new investors AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital and J.P. Morgan.
Rangasayee said the funding would help “catapult” SiMa.ai into a dominant position by giving it the resources to scale its purpose-built platform and compete against incumbent rival Nvidia Corp., which produces more expensive CUDA-based hardware.
The capital raise will fund scaling Palette Neat, the company’s industry-first agentic development environment for Physical AI, and building the next generation of its system-on-chip, Modalix, intended for embedded robotics. SiMa.ai said it is aiming to deliver 1,000 tera operations per second with new hardware in the first half of 2028.
The highest-end Nvidia modules, the Jetson AGX Thor series, hit 2,000 FP4 TOPS and are designed for full-scale humanoid robots and complex autonomous machines. However, mainstream robotic and heavy drone modules such as Jetson T2000 and T3000 cover around 400 and 865 TOPS for mid-tier robotic arms and heavy delivery drones, maintaining a lower power tier to preserve battery life.
As the market-dominant physical AI software, Nvidia’s CUDA-based architecture is also among the most complex and power-hungry. SiMa.ai seeks to offer a lower-power alternative that includes custom-built silicon and software support that can deploy in days or hours.
The company said the next-gen hardware will let it aggressively expand into medium- to high-end drones, humanoid robotics, automotive advanced driver assistance systems and AI-powered cockpits.
Current customers and partners of SiMa.ai include ARK Electronics LLC, AverMedia Technologies Inc., Robert Bosch GmbH, Emerson Electric Co., Micron Technology Co. and Synopsys Inc.

articles.title: Gemini cambia para siempre: su función más útil dejará de existir en noviembre
articles.text:
Una de las primeras funciones populares de Gemini está a punto de cambiar para siempre. Google anunció que las Gems dejarán de existir y migrarán automáticamente a un nuevo sistema de habilidades. Aquellos usuarios que hayan creado y configurado una gema personalizada para trabajar con la IA, tendrán que ajustarse al cambio desde noviembre.
Si usas Gemini y tocas en la opción Gems en el menú lateral, aparecerá un mensaje que indica que las Gems se convertirán en habilidades a partir del 17 de noviembre de 2026. El gigante tecnológico señala que migrará automáticamente todas tus gemas a skills, por lo que en teoría no tendrías que mover un dedo. Debido a que la migración todavía está a más de un mes de distancia, los usuarios de Gemini podrán seguir usándolas hasta que llegue ese día.
En caso de que no estés familiarizado con las Gems, esta fue la primera gran apuesta para adaptar la IA de Google a tus necesidades. En lugar de repetir el prompt cada vez, los usuarios podían guardar instrucciones, añadir contexto y definir el comportamiento del modelo. Esto era muy útil para segmentar las respuestas y enfocar a la IA hacia un solo tema o especialidad, en lugar de tratarla como un asistente general que domina toda clase de información.
De acuerdo con la web de ayuda, Google recreará por su cuenta cada Gem como una habilidad, así que no tendrás que hacer nada si no quieres. Estas habilidades debutaron con Gemini Spark y cumplen el mismo propósito de otorgar instrucciones personalizadas a la IA.
Qué es una habilidad y cuál es la diferencia con una Gem en Gemini
Una habilidad (o Skill) es un conjunto de instrucciones reutilizables que puedes guardar para tareas recurrentes, como aplicar tu estilo de escritura, preparar la agenda de una reunión o plantear un problema desde varias perspectivas. Actualmente, puedes invocar una Skill a través de la barra (/), aunque Google ya está pensando en cambiar ese comando a la @ para facilitar las cosas.
Google menciona que Gemini es capaz de detectar cuando una habilidad encaja con lo que le pides y la aplica sin que la llames. Otro detalle interesante es que puedes apilar varias de estas en una conversación en caso de que necesites resolver una tarea compleja. Esto facilita el flujo que seguíamos con las Gems, que obligaba a abrir el panel lateral, acceder a la sección y buscar entre las gemas guardadas.
Una de sus principales debilidades es que no todas las gemas pueden convertirse en una habilidad, ya que hay funciones que todavía no están disponibles. A diferencia de las Gems, aquí no podrás crear vídeos, música, Canvas, investigaciones profundas o aprendizaje guiado. Lo que sí se puede es combinarlas con aplicaciones conectadas, como las de Google Workspace.
Las gemas de Google dejarán de estar disponibles a partir del 17 de noviembre de 2026. No es necesario que las respaldes, aunque si quieres acceder a las instrucciones y guardarlas, basta con entrar al menú Mis Gems y tocar el ícono de lápiz en aquella que desees. Esto nos llevará a la información de cada Gem, donde podremos descargar las instrucciones en formato de texto plano.

articles.title: Anthropic releases Sonnet 5.5, which it calls a significantly cheaper, faster work partner | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As the AI model wars continue, Anthropic has released the newest version of Sonnet, the company’s mid-tier model, which it says will work much faster (and for significantly less) than its predecessor.
The lab describes Sonnet 5.5 as an ideal assistant for everyday tasks — including coding and creating office documents.
5.5’s predecessor, Sonnet 5, was announced about three months ago. At the time, the model’s selling point was efficient agentic deployment — the ability to run agents at a lower cost than competitors.
The big selling point with 5.5, meanwhile, is speed. Anthropic claims that Sonnet 5.5 is 30 percent faster than its predecessor, and that its rate of token burn is significantly slower.
In the Anthropic hierarchy of models, Sonnet is less powerful than the Opus model, but can be more useful in certain circumstances because its agility. In particular, Anthropic’s benchmarks show Sonnet 5.5 performing better than Opus 5.5 on agentic coding, likely because of its ability to spawn multiple agents without exceeding cost limits.
Sonnet 5.5 is also said to have significant cyber capabilities, with the company claiming that it has “comparable” cyber capabilities to Opus 5. As a result, Anthropic says that 5.5 is the first Sonnet model that will be subject the same cyber safeguards that apply to Fable and Opus.
The company also plans to release a new version of Haiku — its smallest model — in the coming weeks, although it didn’t give a firm date as to when that would happen.
The last year has seen a flurry of new model releases from the major AI labs. Just last week, OpenAI released a number of new models — including enhanced versions of Sol and Luna, its mid-tier and budget-friendly models. Meta also announced a new model, which it said would power an upcoming feature associated with its smart glasses.

articles.title: 'My favorite headphones of 2026': I tested the Sonos Ace Ultra vs the Sony WH-1000XM6, and it was a true headphones battle for the ages — here's my winner based on real-world use
articles.text:
I tested the Sonos Ace Ultra against the Sony WH-1000XM6 and it was a closer contest than I'd expected — here’s which noise cancelling headphones came out on top
Two top-tier headphones, only one winner
With a significant improvement in musicality, excellent Dolby Atmos performance, and a more fleshed-out feature set, the Sonos Ace Ultra feel like a big improvement over their predecessor. Incremental additions to battery life, ANC, and Sonos ecosystem interactivity only help these stylish cans to stand-out more than the original model. While the Ace Ultra may still get edged out by a few rivals in terms of sonic detail and travel convenience, they’re still easy to recommend.
Pros
- Excellent audio for movies
- Good Sonos ecosystem interactivity
- Stellar look and great build quality
Cons
- Not fully foldable, like the XM6
- No LDAC support
- Don’t sound quite as detailed
The Sony WH-1000XM6 are a fantastic pair of over-ear headphones that combine the best design elements of their predecessors, while levelling up the sonic and ANC capabilities of what came before. With super-clean touch controls, an ultra-comfy fit and a ton of features at your disposal, there’s a lot to love about these headphones – though they do look a little bulky.
Pros
- Class-leading ANC
- Fantastic sound quality
- Incredibly intuitive touch controls
Cons
- Slightly weaker battery life
- Bulkier look than the Ace Ultra
- No Snapdragon Sound/aptX support
The Sonos Ace Ultra just dropped, and they might just be my favorite headphones of 2026. They’re a considerable upgrade over the original Ace, boasting far better musicality, incredible movie audio, expanded Sonos ecosystem support, and seriously good ANC. It really feels like Sonos has made a statement with this release, and the multi-room specialist is finally ready to take on the titans of the headphone world.
But just how well do the Sonos Ace Ultra shape up against their class-leading rivals at this money? I wanted to find out for myself, so I tested them against one of their fiercest competitors: the Sony WH-1000XM6. Sony’s flagship headphones come in at the same price point as the Ace Ultra and they too supply stellar sound, noise-crushing ANC, and a swathe of fantastic features.
So, which headphones are better: the Sonos Ace Ultra or the Sony WH-1000XM6? I’ve compared them across four key areas: features, sound quality, design, and value, to help you decide which are the best headphones for you. The Sony WH-1000XM6 have been my go-to headphones for well over a year, but this contest was genuinely far closer than I’d expected. But anyway, let the battle commence — oh, and make sure to stick around 'til the end, for my verdict.
Sonos Ace Ultra vs Sony WH-1000XM6: price & availability
The Sonos Ace Ultra were released in September 2026, about two years after the original Sonos Ace headphones arrived on the scene. The Ace Ultra cost $449 / £399 / AU$699, which is cheaper than the standard model cost at launch in the UK, and the same price as the original Ace launched at in both the US and Australia.
Meanwhile, the Sony WH-1000XM6 are a little older, and hit the market back in May 2025. They cost the same as the Sonos Ace Ultra, carrying a price tag of $449 / £399 / AU$699. As they’ve been about for a little longer, it’s more likely that you’ll find these cans on sale, and we have seen them drop below $380 / £300 / AU$500 before. While neither of these models are cheap, they both offer incredible quality across the board, with excellent sound quality and features, which helps to justify the steep asking price.
Sonos Ace Ultra vs Sony WH-1000XM6: specs
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Sonos Ace Ultra | Sony WH-1000XM6 | 
|---|---|---|
| Price | $449 / £399 / AU$699 | $449 / £399 / AU$699 | 
| Drivers | Next-gen 40mm custom | 30mm dynamic | 
| Active noise cancellation | Yes | Yes | 
| Battery life | 35 hours | 30 hours | 
| Weight | 322g | 254g | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 6.0, USB-C | Bluetooth 5.4, 3.5mm | 
| Frequency range | 20Hz-20kHz | 20Hz-20kHz | 
Sonos Ace Ultra vs Sony WH-1000XM6: features
Let me be clear from the offset: when it comes to features, these two pairs of wireless headphones are arguably the very best on the market. So, as you can imagine, it’s hard to pick a winner here.
The Sonos Ace Ultra and Sony WH-1000XM6 share a lot of the same positives: they each have extensive EQ options, with multi-band custom options, wired and Bluetooth connectivity, wear detection, and impressive ANC.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
When it comes to noise-cancelling specifically, both are excellent performers, and easily dispose of external sounds like surrounding chatter and traffic noise. In my testing, I found the Sony WH-1000XM6 to have a very slight edge, though, perhaps lending to their larger microphone system (12 mics to the Ace Ultra’s 10) — they dulled deep sounds like engines rumbling to slightly greater effect.
Something that the Sonos Ace supply that Sony can’t compete with, is wider ecosystem support. TV Audio Linking enables you to transfer audio from a compatible Sonos soundbar and enjoy immersive sound privately, while Headphone Linking gives you the option to hand off audio to supported speakers, including the Sonos Play (or vice versa) for a seamless listening experience, no matter where you are.
Another thing that I love about the Ace Ultra is their native Dolby Atmos support. This means you can enjoy Dolby Atmos music and movies at their very best, and with the help of head-tracking, I’ve been able to enjoy deliciously expansive movie audio with impressive height effects and clear dialogue to boot. The Sony WH-1000XM6 aren’t as accomplished for movies, and while they feature a Cinema upmix mode, which transfers a stereo signal into a more expansive format, the actual quality of this is a little disappointing.
While we’re on the topic of sound-related features, it’s worth talking about codecs. Each of these headphones possesses something the other does not. And that’s because the Sonos Ace Ultra boast aptX codec support — something Sony skips on — while the XM6 feature LDAC, which their competitor leaves out. Both of these open up higher-res Bluetooth streaming, opening up a more detailed listen than you’d get with SBC or AAC, for instance.
The key differentiator here is compatibility. Apple fans, I’m sorry, but your phone supports neither of these. Android users, there’s a very high chance that your handset can make use of LDAC, which is actually a proprietary technology developed by Sony itself. However, it’s a different story with aptX. Fewer phones support this, and although I get to enjoy it on my Xiaomi 17, a lot of models leave it out. Both models support lossless wired listening, although only Sonos has USB-C audio passthrough, which is more convenient in my view — after all, so many of us carry around USB-C cables to charge our phones and other devices
In terms of battery life, these cans are close, but Sonos is the overall winner. The Ace Ultra provide 35 hours of playback with ANC switched on, whereas Sony give you 30 hours. That’s a pretty average amount of playtime to get from headphones in this price-class, but if you do run out of charge, you can use both pairs while they regain life via USB-C.
Finally, a word on controls. The Sonos Ace Ultra feature responsive, well-sized, and precise button controls. But they don’t have touch controls, something the WH-100XM6 pull off brilliantly. Sony’s cans have reactive and intuitive touch controls that I love. A single press won’t trigger anything so you can avoid accidental commands, but you can swipe on the right earcup to adjust playback and even cover it with your hand to enter into transparency mode. As much as I appreciate the reliability of Sonos’ buttons, I prefer Sony’s approach.
So, who’s the winner in the features category? It’s such a close one: I think Sony has a slight edge in ANC, I like the touch controls, and the broader compatibility of LDAC is a win. However, Sonos’ ecosystem interplay, native Atmos support, USB-C audio, and better battery life is pretty impressive too. Let’s call this category a tie.
Sonos Ace Ultra vs Sony WH-1000XM6: sound quality
While both of these headphones sound great, and there’s not a big different in quality, there’s only one winner for me.
The Sonos Ace Ultra made a big step up from the original Ace, especially when it comes to musicality. They provide well-balanced sound, with satisfyingly deep, regimented bass, clean mids, and expressive highs. But how do they compete against the Sony WH-1000XM6?
Well, allow me to reference my listening notes. In the funk tack, Joía rara by Brylho, both sets kept electric guitars well-separated from vocals and other instruments in the mid-range, almost making it sound as if they were playing in a unique pocket. Both also plated up well-weighted, clean bass, and finer details, like subtle percussive elements came through nicely. I did find, though, that the XM6 handled vocals with a bit more care — they sounded a bit more natural, and more effectively defined in the mix.
Moving onto a house track next, with Get it on by Jansons. This was a tight contest, the Ace Ultra’s deep bass came through with palpable impact, and higher-pitched drums sounded tastefully forward without getting shrill or tinny. It was the same on the XM6 — thumping yet agile bass alongside bright and precise treble, helping to capture the exciting, energetic vibe. I perhaps found that the XM6 offered slightly better dynamism, though — drops just had a bit more impact, which isn’t to say that the Ace fell flat, they were just marginally outclassed.
More generally, I found that the XM6 slightly edged out the Ace Ultra with more dynamic low-end output and better detailing, especially in the mid-range.
It’s worth noting that I do consider the Ace Ultra to be superior for movies. They have native Dolby Atmos support, and with built-in head-tracking, you can experience truly mesmerizing audio for all your movie-watching needs. When I connected the headphones up to the Sonos Beam Ultra via TV Audio Swap, I was blown away by the fidelity of height effects, the phenomenal width, and clear dialogue available. Sony’s headphones are good for movies, and they do feature some head-tracking technology (albeit more restrictive), but the Ace Ultra were clearly designed with movies in mind to a much greater extent.
Still, it’s important to have some perspective. The vast majority of people aren’t buying wireless headphones solely to watch movies. The most important thing is portable musical performance, and while the Sonos Ace Ultra get close to the Sony WH-1000XM6, they fall just short overall — and as a result, I’m handing Sony the W here.
Sonos Ace Ultra vs Sony WH-1000XM6: design
At a glance, these headphones might not look wildly different, especially as I tested two very similar colorways… but there are some notable deviations worth discussing.
In my view, the Sonos Ace Ultra are the better looking pair of headphones. They have a slimmer form factor with flatter ear cups, which look a bit more flattering than the XM6’s bulky ones. Their metallic details and curved look also gives them a premium yet understated aesthetic which I can’t get enough of.
The XM6 aren’t bad-looking at all, I just don’t think they quite match the luxurious vibe of the Ace Ultra. But what I do like about these is that they’re fully foldable. This means they’re amazing for travel — just fold’ em up, throw them in your bag, and you’re good to go. The ear cups can fold down on the Ace, enabling them to fit in their carry case, but they’re not quite as flexible as Sony’s flagship model.
On the topic of cases, Sony takes the win here. They have an enticing hard case which uses a magnet lock, meaning it’s so quick and easy to whip them out or stow them away. The Ace Ultra’s case doesn’t have the same premium feel, and it also has a pretty low-quality zip that jams a bit too regularly for my liking.
Neither of these models have an IP rating, which denotes dust and waterproofing capabilities — something that, in fairness, is rarely seen on over-ears (though some, like the Noble FoKus Artemis, do boast an IP rating).
But both models are very comfortable and don’t clamp too hard on my head, which makes it easy to listen to music for hours on end. This means they’re pretty close overall in the design section, but personally, I’d take the sleeker look and more luxurious design of the Ace Ultra over the XM6 — even if the latter are fully foldable and have a better carry case.
Sonos Ace Ultra vs Sony WH-1000XM6: value
So, it’s been a tight contest so far. And when you consider that both the Ace Ultra and XM6 have the same list price, deciding which offers better value for money is very tough indeed.
The truth is this: the better-value model is going to be very dependent on your needs and expectations. If you already own a Sonos system, and want interplay with your speakers and maybe even a soundbar, then the Ace Ultra are incredibly attractive. Their ANC and sound quality isn’t far off the XM6’s, they’re superior for movies, and I think they’re more stylish too.
But if you want the best all-round pair of headphones in this price bracket, I still don’t think you can beat the Sony WH-1000XM6 right now. They offer slightly more detailed, dynamic audio than the Ace Ultra, their ANC is class-leading, and they have no shortage of features, a fully foldable design, and their battery life is close to that of their Sonos rival.
In the context of this showdown, the XM6’s older age also works in their favor somewhat — we’ve seen them go on sale a few times here and there, so chances are, you’ll be able to swipe them up for less than the Ace Ultra in practice. I think you’ll be exceedingly happy with either of these models, but unless you want interplay with your Sonos system and top-tier Atmos for movies, then I think the Sony WH-1000XM6 give you ever-so-slightly more bang for your buck.
Sonos Ace Ultra vs Sony WH-1000XM6: verdict
So, there you have it. As I mentioned in the value section, it’s been a close affair, but I think the Sony WH-1000XM6 are the best headphones for most people at the time of writing. Ultimately, their marginal wins over Sonos in terms of ANC, musicality, and flexibility give them the edge.
If you have a Sonos system, though, I do think the Ace Ultra are worth picking for their seamless connectivity with your speakers and soundbar. And the Ace Ultra do offer a few improvements over Sony’s cans, like higher battery life, a more luxurious look, and better sound for movies.
Both are great options, however, so you can feel confident in your choice, whether you opt for Sonos or Sony. But what do you think? Would you choose the Sonos Ace Ultra or Sony WH-1000XM6? Let me know in the comments.

articles.title: UK government tells staff to stop thanking AI chatbots — draft guidance pushes lightweight models and shorter prompts to cut environmental impact
articles.text:
UK government tells staff to stop thanking AI chatbots — draft guidance pushes lightweight models and shorter prompts to cut environmental impact
It's more efficient not to say thank you, and there's just no need to, the document explains, alongside other best practices.
The United Kingdom government has published a guide on how its employees should use AI, including a reminder that people don't need to thank their chatbots for their work. The new document, which is still a draft and yet to be finalized, is designed to help people use AI "safely, fairly and sustainably, especially for government work."
The draft "Using AI ethically and sustainably" document also warns users that they should check and follow any AI policies put in place by their individual departments, noting that there may be specific tools and approaches that they should use. It's unclear which departments these may be, but it suggests an awareness that usage patterns may change depending on the nature of the work being done. This is backed up by a section that reminds employees to use the right tool for the task. Examples include using Gemini Flash instead of Gemini Pro and GPT Instant instead of GPT Thinking.
The sub-600-word document offers guidance on using AI responsibly, including checking the output of an AI before using it. This doesn't just apply to making sure that any actual data the AI provides is correct, but also includes ensuring that "users or groups are treated fairly and equally" as well as avoiding "stereotypes or discriminatory language."
The government is also keen to make sure that its employees don't rely on AI, reminding everyone that they are responsible for any content or decisions that are made using the input of AI. They won't be able to simply point the finger at an AI-powered tool if something goes awry. This is especially notable given a recent report suggested that using AI can actually increase burnout because it allows workers to take on too many tasks.
The "Use AI efficiently" section is where the document aims to help reduce the environmental impact of AI use — including a reminder that users need not say thank you. Further, they're told that they should use as few prompts as possible while ensuring they are as short, clear, and direct as possible. There's also a (dead) link to a prompt library. It's possible that the link is only available to those on a government network.
It is, of course, true that you don't need to thank a chatbot for its help, but some may choose to ignore that advice. Especially given constant claims by AI companies that their tech "could kill all humans" sooner or later.

articles.title: Japón y Rusia terminaron la Segunda Guerra Mundial hace 81 años. Con un pequeño detalle: nunca firmaron la paz por culpa de cuatro islas
articles.text:
Japón y Rusia llevan 81 años viviendo una anomalía diplomática difícil de encontrar en otro lugar del mundo. La Segunda Guerra Mundial terminó en 1945 y ambos países restablecieron sus relaciones diplomáticas en 1956, pero nunca consiguieron firmar el tratado de paz que debía cerrar definitivamente aquel capítulo. El obstáculo cabe prácticamente en un mapa pequeño: cuatro territorios controlados por Rusia y reclamados por Japón. El conflicto parecía condenado a ir apagándose con el paso de las generaciones, hasta que Vladimir Putin decidió este verano hacer algo por primera vez en sus 25 años en el poder.
Cuando la guerra terminó. La raíz está en las últimas semanas de 1945. La Unión Soviética entró en guerra contra Japón y sus tropas ocuparon estas islas alrededor de la capitulación japonesa, incorporándolas posteriormente al territorio soviético. Allí vivían entonces alrededor de 17.000 japoneses, con decenas de escuelas y comunidades dedicadas principalmente a la pesca.
Algunos huyeron y la mayoría de quienes permanecieron terminaron siendo expulsados mientras llegaban nuevos habitantes soviéticos. Tokio considera que las cuatro islas forman sus Territorios del Norte y nunca aceptó su incorporación a la URSS. Moscú sostiene que las Kuriles meridionales pasaron legítimamente a soberanía soviética como resultado de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Esa incompatibilidad territorial acabó sobreviviendo a la propia guerra.
A dos islas de solucionarlo. Japón y la URSS firmaron en 1956 una declaración conjunta que puso fin formalmente al estado de guerra y restauró las relaciones diplomáticas, pero dejaron pendiente el verdadero tratado de paz. Moscú aceptó que Habomai y Shikotan fueran entregadas a Japón después de firmarlo, mientras que las diferencias sobre Kunashiri y Etorofu quedaron sin resolver.
La fórmula nunca llegó a ejecutarse y las cuatro islas continuaron bajo control soviético. Tras la desaparición de la URSS hubo nuevos intentos de desencallar el problema, y en 2001 Putin y el entonces primer ministro japonés Yoshiro Mori volvieron a reconocer la declaración de 1956 como punto de partida de las negociaciones.
20 veces con Putin. Cuando Abe regresó al poder en 2012 convirtió el acercamiento con Moscú en una de sus grandes apuestas diplomáticas. Se reunió alrededor de una veintena de veces con el jefe de Rusia, impulsó cooperación económica e incluso trató de mantener margen de maniobra con Rusia después de la anexión de Crimea en 2014.
Nada consiguió romper el bloqueo. Al mismo tiempo, Moscú fue reforzando militarmente las islas y dejando cada vez más claro que no contemplaba devolverlas en los términos reclamados por Tokio.
Entonces llegó Ucrania. La invasión rusa de Ucrania en 2022 cambió radicalmente el escenario. Japón se sumó a las sanciones contra Moscú y endureció su lenguaje sobre los Territorios del Norte. Rusia respondió suspendiendo las negociaciones del tratado de paz y los programas que permitían a antiguos habitantes japoneses visitar las islas y las tumbas de sus familiares.
Cuatro años después, el Gobierno japonés mantiene oficialmente que quiere resolver la soberanía de los cuatro territorios para poder concluir finalmente el tratado, pero reconoce que las relaciones bilaterales atraviesan una situación especialmente complicada por la guerra de Ucrania.
La “jugada” de Putin. El conflicto congelado volvió a calentarse el 13 de agosto de 2026, cuando Putin visitó Etorofu por primera vez desde que llegó al poder. Japón protestó inmediatamente y calificó el viaje de incompatible con su posición territorial, mientras Rusia ha acompañado esa demostración política con ejercicios militares y un creciente despliegue en la zona.
Tokio sostiene que esa militarización es inaceptable y ha reiterado que su objetivo continúa siendo resolver la atribución de las cuatro islas y firmar el tratado pendiente. Sobre el papel sigue existiendo una negociación. Sobre el terreno, Rusia administra el archipiélago y acaba de subrayarlo con la presencia física de su presidente.
Rusia a solo 3 km. Ese lugar es Nemuro, una ciudad pesquera situada en el extremo oriental de Hokkaido. Desde el cabo Nosappu apenas 3,7 kilómetros de agua separan Japón de la parte más próxima de los territorios controlados por Rusia, y en días despejados las islas aparecen directamente frente a la costa. Allí siguen viviendo algunos de quienes fueron expulsados siendo niños, aunque su número se desploma: quedan unos 4.700 antiguos residentes en todo Japón y su edad media ronda ya los 90 años.
Las visitas a los cementerios de sus familias están suspendidas, así que algunos han terminado rezando y depositando flores desde barcos frente a unas islas a las que ya no pueden regresar. Japón considera precisamente la reanudación de esas visitas una de sus prioridades inmediatas con Moscú.
La firma que no llega. Si se quiere, la paradoja es que Japón y Rusia comercian, mantienen relaciones diplomáticas y llevan generaciones sin combatir entre sí. Lo que no tienen es ese tratado de paz definitivo porque ninguna negociación ha conseguido resolver qué hacer con cuatro territorios cuya superficie resulta minúscula frente al tamaño de Rusia y Japón, pero cuyo valor histórico, estratégico y económico es enorme para ambos.
En 1945, aquellas islas quedaron atrapadas entre dos países que estaban terminando una guerra mundial; 81 años después siguen exactamente ahí, ahora rodeadas por sanciones, ejercicios militares y otra guerra que ha vuelto a enfrentar a Rusia con buena parte de los aliados de Japón. El mundo cerró hace décadas la Segunda Guerra Mundial.
Entre Tokio y Moscú todavía queda una firma pendiente.
Imagen | Tennen-Gas, Associate professor , 1467jp

articles.title: Google Messages change la manière de répondre aux messages
articles.text:
Après avoir réinventé son copier-coller, l’application de messagerie de Google revoit sa copie dans sa dernière mise à jour, actuellement en cours de déploiement. Si vous utilisez l’application au quotidien, ces modifications vont sûrement vous demander un petit temps d’adaptation.
Un nouveau geste pour afficher l’heure de publication des messages
Consulter l’heure exacte à laquelle un message a été envoyé demandait jusqu’à présent de taper directement sur la bulle de discussion. Cela permettait aussi d’afficher les accusés de réception ou le cadenas qui indique le chiffrement RCS. Désormais, il suffit de balayer vers la gauche depuis n’importe où dans la conversation pour faire apparaitre les horaires de chaque message ainsi que le statut du cryptage. Un regroupement des informations qui évite d’avoir à inspecter les bulles une par une.
Pour vous aider à comprendre le nouveau fonctionnement, Google Messages affiche un petit indice visuel : un appui rapide sur un message reçu fait brièvement ressortir les horodatages pour vous montrer comment interagir avec. Les accusés de réception de vos messages restent quant à eux accessibles en touchant simplement le message concerné.
Une nouvelle méthode pour répondre aux messages
Répondre directement à un message demande d’inverser le mouvement habituel puisqu’il faut désormais glisser vers la droite directement sur la bulle en question. Cela demande peu de précision pour que l’application comprenne la manipulation du premier coup.
Un mouvement vers la droite permet désormais de répondre rapidement à un message. – © 01net
Dans le même temps, l’interface graphique montre quelques bizarreries avec le retour du design classique à deux cercles au lieu de la version épurée testée pendant des mois. Cette petite incohérence s’affiche un peu partout, que ce soit sur l’écran d’accueil ou sur la page de détails d’une conversation. Google remettra peut-être un peu d’ordre dans tout ça à l’occasion d’une prochaine mise à jour.
Sur le même sujet : Google Messages va avoir droit à une refonte de son moteur de recherche
